postings.conferenceText: GreenMM: Efficient Systems and AI for the PlanetWorkshop at ACM Multimedia 2026 (ACM MM 2026), Rio de Janeiro, BrazilGreenMM brings together researchers working on efficient multimedia AI systems and multimedia AI for environmental and planetary applications. The workshop focuses on building multimedia models that are both technically strong and environmentally responsible. Multimedia AI spans vision, video, audio, language, and multimodal learning. It is now one of the most computationally demanding areas of AI, while also becoming central to biodiversity monitoring, climate analysis, environmental sensing, agriculture, and disaster response.Topics of interest include, but are not limited to:Efficient and Sustainable Multimedia AI Systems- Energy and memory efficient video and multimodal architectures- Efficient vision language and multimodal foundation models- Compression, pruning, quantization, and distillation for multimedia- Sparse, adaptive, and token reduction methods for vision and video- Parameter efficient fine tuning for large multimodal models- Efficient generative models for image, audio, and video- Carbon aware training, scheduling, and deployment- Resource efficient inference for edge and real time systems- Data efficient learning under limited annotations- Benchmarking and reporting of energy and carbon footprintMultimedia AI for Environmental and Planetary Applications- Vision and video analysis for biodiversity and wildlife monitoring- Acoustic and audio based monitoring of ecosystems and species- Satellite and aerial imagery analysis for land use and climate change- Environmental change detection in long term multimodal streams- AI for precision agriculture and sustainable food systems- Multimedia sensing for water, air, and soil quality- Disaster monitoring and climate risk analysis- Vision language models for environmental reporting- Low cost, scalable sensing systems for environmental monitoring- Integration of video, audio, satellite, and text dataSubmission FormatProspective authors are invited to submit high quality full papers representing original results. Submissions will follow the ACM MM 2026 format and must adhere to the main conference submission style, format, length restrictions, and camera ready timeline.Submission link: https://openreview.net/group?id=acmmm.org/ACMMM/2026/Workshop/GreenMMWorkshop website: https://sites.google.com/view/greenmm-workshop/home

postings.conferenceText: Methods of analytical and stochastic modelling are widely used in engineering to assess and design various complex systems, like computer and communication networks, and manufacturing systems. The ASMTA conference is a main forum for advancing these techniques and their applications and aims to bring together researchers of academia and industry to discuss the latest developments in analytical, numerical and simulation algorithms for stochastic systems.This year, the conference will be held as a workshop within IFIP WG 7.3 Performance 2026 in Ghent, Belgium.ASMTA 2026 seeks both methodological papers that propose novel analytical and numerical solution techniques for stochastic systems, as well as application-oriented papers that apply stochastic modelling techniques to practical performance problems. The website for ASMTA 2026 will be at https://asmta.github.io. Submissions will be on Microsoft CMT at https://cmt3.research.microsoft.com/ASMTA2026The proceedings of ASMTA 2026 will be published in the Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science (LNCS) series. Submissions may already be prepared in LNCS format and must not exceed 15 pages, including figures, tables, and references; see the information for authors on Springer as web site for formatting instructions (Springer).A selection of the best papers will be invited to submit a fast-tracked extended version of the work to the Performance Evaluation (PEVA) journal.Important DatesPaper submission deadline: August 28, 2026 (Extended, FIRM)Notification of acceptance: September 11, 2026OrganisationTPC Chairs:Illés Horváth Budapest University of Technology and Economics, HungaryVincenzo Mancuso, University of Palermo, Italy & IMDEA Networks Institute, Madrid, SpainScope and TopicsASMTA 2026 seeks both methodological papers that propose novel analytical and numerical solution techniques for stochastic systems, as well as application-oriented papers that apply stochastic modelling techniques to practical performance problems. Topics of interest include the following.Performance-Oriented Methodologies:Markov ProcessesQueueing Systems and NetworksCapacity Planning, Resource Allocation, Routing, Scheduling and Quality of ServiceBranching Processes and Epidemic ModelsGame Theory and Stochastic GamesReliability Theory(Computationally Intensive) Statistical MethodsStochastic Control, Decision Processes and OptimisationRare Events and Stochastic SimulationApproximations, Bounds and Limits of Stochastic ModelsReinforcement Learning Techniques for Dynamic Resource AllocationFluid and Diffusion LimitsRandom GraphsEnvisaged Application Areas:Complex SystemsComputer and Information SystemsWorkflow Management SystemsCommunication Systems and NetworksWireless and Mobile Systems and NetworksPeer-to-Peer Applications and ServicesEmbedded Systems and Sensor NetworksStorage Systems, Data Centres, Content Delivery, Cloud/Fog/EdgeWorkload Modelling and CharacterisationRoad Traffic and TransportationSocial NetworksModelling of VirtualisationEnergy-Aware OptimisationStochastic Modelling for Systems BiologyBiologically Inspired Network DesignArtificial Intelligence and Machine Learning PlatformsBlockchains and Crypto-CurrencyNetwork Economics and Platform DesignsMatching Systems and Sharing EconomySubmissionSubmissions will be on Microsoft CMT at https://cmt3.research.microsoft.com/ASMTA2026The Microsoft CMT service was used for managing the peer-reviewing process for this conference. This service was provided for free by Microsoft and they bore all expenses, including costs for Azure cloud services as well as for software development and support.

postings.conferenceText: The Technical Committee of the 11th International Conference on Cyber Security and Information Engineering (ICCSIE 2026) invites the submission of original research papers in the fields of theoretical, experimental, and applied cyber security and information engineering to be published in the conference proceedings. Each submission is anonymously reviewed by an average of three independent reviewers, to ensure the final high standard and quality of submitted papers. Accepted papers will be presented as either oral or poster at the conference.Contributions are sought in the following areas:Cyber SecuritySecurity & Privacy in Wired, Wireless, Mobile, Hybrid, Sensor, Ad Hoc NetworksNetwork Intrusion Detection and Prevention, Firewalls, Packet FiltersCommunication Privacy and AnonymityDistributed Denial of ServicePublic Key Infrastructures, Key Peer-to-Peer and Overlay Network SystemsInformation Leakage & Information TheftData Tampering & DeletionEncrypted CommunicationInformation Dissemination SafetyApplication SecurityEmail EngineeringCommunications EngineeringManagement Information SystemNetwork Management & PerformanceMeasurement & Integrated Wiring TechnologyInformation DisplayPhotoelectric Technology & Photoelectric Information EngineeringInformation Warfare TechnologyIntegrated Circuit DesignDigital Media Technology & Radio/Television EngineeringDetection Guidance & Control TechnologyElectromagnetic Field & Adaptive Antenna Array System & Network System ProjectIntelligence Science and TechnologyDigital Signal ProcessingWireless CommunicationInformation Engineering & Communications Engineering & Program-Controlled Exchange TechnologyVideo Transmission/Analysis & Visual Information ProcessingIntegration SystemCommunication Theory & Communication SystemOther Related TopicsImportant DatesLast date for paper submission: July 31, 2026Last date for paper acceptance: August 31, 2026Last date for registration: September 10, 2026PublicationAll accepted and registered papers will be published by IEEE, and will be sent to included by IEEE Xplore, EI Compendex and Scopus.Submission GuidelinesAll submissions should be in English and range from 4 to 8 pages, including figures and references, and should be formatted according to the template, which will be sent to you upon acceptance.Please email your papers to iccisie@iaast.cn. To avoid duplicate submissions, kindly use only one method.Authors are required to complete their submissions before the designated deadlines, as late submissions will not be considered. Both initial and final submissions should be in an editable format; hard copies will not be accepted.The latest information can be found on the conference website.Review InstructionICCSIE 2026 follows the highest standards of publication ethics and takes all possible procedures against any publication misconduct. This Conference does not accept any type of plagiarism, which means that any author replicating a significant part of another's work without acknowledging him/her or passing another's work off as his/her own is not tolerated and not published.All authors submitting their works to ICCSIE 2026 for publication as original works confirm that the submitted papers are their own contributions and have not been copied in whole or in part from other works.Each submission is anonymously reviewed by an average of three independent reviewers, to ensure the final high standard and quality of each accepted submission. The ICCSIE 2026 guarantees that the entire peer review and publication process is meticulous and objective. Furthermore, all works not in accordance with these standards will be removed from publication if malpractice is revealed at any time even after the publication. Every case of suspected plagiarism or duplicate publishing will be reported.

postings.conferenceName: International Conference on High Performance Computing in Asia-Pacific Region
postings.conferenceText: ====================================================================                            Call for Papers                   2027 International Conference on    High Performance Computing in Asia-Pacific Region (HPC Asia 2027)                         February 17-19, 2027                             Seoul, Korea                      https://hpcasia2027.org/====================================================================*** Call for Papers Submission ***High-performance computing (HPC) plays a crucial role in tackling large and complex problems in artificial intelligence, science, engineering, and business by employing efficient algorithms, applications, systems, and software for massively parallel and distributed computing systems and data centers. The International Conference on High Performance Computing in the Asia-Pacific Region (HPC Asia) has established itself as a premier forum for researchers and professionals to exchange ideas and nurture innovation across all aspects of high-performance computing systems and applications. We solicit original contributions, all of which undergo rigorous peer review. Specific topics of interest include but are not limited to the following research tracks below.====================================================================*** Submission Timeline **** Submission of Paper: September 27, 2026 (Firm Deadline)* Notice of Paper Acceptance: November 22, 2026* Camera-ready Paper Due: January 08, 2026* Conference: February 17 - 19, 2027HPC Asia has only one deadline for the submission of abstracts and papers. Authors are welcome to submit abstracts at any time up to the paper submission deadline. To ensure a smooth process, please submit both abstracts and papers together using the same Linklings submission form before the specified deadline.====================================================================*** Topics of Interests ***1. Applications & Algorithms   * High performance applications   * Computational science   * Numerical linear algebra and its applications   * Parallel and vectorization algorithms   * Hybrid/heterogeneous/accelerated algorithms   * Fault-tolerant algorithms   * Graph algorithms   * Algorithms and applications for AI or quantum computing2. Hardware Systems & Architectures   * Processor architecture advancements   * Accelerator technologies (GPUs, FPGAs, ASICs)   * Network architecture and interconnects   * Memory hierarchy and management   * Energy-efficient processor and accelerator design   * Dependable and fault-tolerant architectures   * Integration of new technologies in processor and network design   * Emerging hardware systems for AI or quantum computing3. Programming Models & System Software   * Programming languages and compilation techniques   * Programming models and runtime for future novel systems   * Tools and libraries for performance and productivity   * Performance portability   * System management, resource management and scheduler   * Techniques for testing, debugging, reproducibility and determinism   * Techniques for fault tolerance and energy efficiency   * Programming models and system software for AI or quantum computing4. Data, Storage & Visualization   * Big data processing and analytics   * Distributed and parallel file systems   * Storage architectures and systems   * Data provenance, traceability, and reproducibility   * High-performance I/O and storage optimization   * Data visualization techniques and image processing in HPC   * Cross-cutting methods of AI with the above topics====================================================================*** Online Submission System ***Authors submitting papers for HPC Asia 2027 must submit them via Linklings. Submitted papers must contain original work that has not appeared in and is not under consideration for another conference or journal. The review process is double-blind. There will be no revision/rebuttal process and the review will be one-pass.* Submission URL: https://ssl.linklings.net/conferences/HPCAsia/====================================================================*** Submission Format ***All authors should submit manuscripts for review in a two-column format. Manuscripts must be at 8 to 10 pages in PDF format including figures and references, formatted according to the ACM ProceedingsStyle. Templates are provided via the conference webpage.====================================================================*** Proceedings ***The proceedings will be published in the ACM Digital Library.====================================================================

postings.conferenceText: The 3rd International Workshop on Artificial Intelligence for Cybersecurity (AI-SEC-2027),in conjunction with the 41th International Conference on Advanced Information Networking and Applications (AINA-2027) Conference,Polytechnic University of Tirana, Albania (remote participation is possible), March 24-26 2027.https://sites.google.com/community.unipa.it/ai-sec-2027/home •********************************************************************************About the Workshop: The AI-SEC 2027 workshop aims to bring together researchers, industry professionals, and practitioners to discuss the latest advancements in artificial intelligence for cybersecurity. The workshop will focus on innovative AI techniques and real-world applications that strengthen system and network security, counter evolving cyber threats, and ensure the robustness of AI models in distributed environments.Topics of Interest: All topics related to the contribution of artificial intelligence approaches to the security of networks and distributed systems are welcome. These include, but are not limited to:• Privacy-preserving AI and data security in distributed computing• AI-assisted authentication and zero-trust network access control• AI-enhanced Trust Management in Multi-agent Systems• AI-assisted techniques for malware and intrusion detection• AI for the detection of threats and anomalies in Software-defined Networking• AI-based context-aware network diagnostic and threat detection• Network forensic analysis and incident response using AI• AI-assisted techniques for security in web applications• AI-based fault tolerance in distributed systems• AI for physical layer and cross-layer security• Applications of AI methods for wireless and mobile securityLightweight AI models for resource-constrained security in IoT and edge/pervasive networksAI-enhanced security for Mobile Ad-hoc Networks and Wearable SystemsAI-enabled attacks and countermeasuresAdversarial robustness and model security in distributed computing systemsPoisoning attacks and Byzantine-robust defenses in decentralized AISUBMISSION GUIDELINESWe welcome research paper up to 10 pages in length, including all figures, tables, and references. Papers must be prepared using the Lecture Notes Style of Springer Proceedings (template available here: https://voyager.ce.fit.ac.jp/conf/aina/2027/public/For-the-authors-LECTURE-NOTES-TEMPLATES.zip), and must be formatted in PDF format.For detailed submission instructions, please visit https://voyager.ce.fit.ac.jp/conf/aina/2027/Papersummit.Paper submission link: https://edas.info/N35435.All accepted papers will be included in the conference proceedings of the Lecture Notes series published by Springer. Proceedings will be sent by Springer for indexing in SCOPUS. Authors of accepted papers will be given instructions for submitting the camera-ready version and the copyright form.IMPORTANT DATESSubmission Deadline: December 10, 2026Author Notification: January 10, 2027Camera-Ready Submission: January 25, 2027

postings.conferenceName: [Call for Participation] AstroCLIMB Shared Task — Multimodal Citation Linking @ WASP 2026 (AACL-IJCNLP)
postings.conferenceText: ====================================================================CALL FOR PARTICIPATIONAstroCLIMB: Astronomy Citation Linking from Illustrations,a Multimodal BenchmarkShared task of the 4th Workshop on Artificial Intelligence forScientific Publications (WASP 2026), co-located with IJCNLP-AACL 2026Workshop: November 10, 2026 (online)Task page: https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/WIESP/2026/shared_taskKaggle competition: https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/astroclimb/overviewDataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/adsabs/AstroCLIMB====================================================================OVERVIEWScientists rely on figures to communicate their results, yet the information locked in those figures is hard to parse, archive, and search. Recent multimodal models promise to change that, but they have seen little testing on real scientific figures. AstroCLIMB, built in partnership with astroexplorer.org, offers a benchmark to probe exactly this capability: can a model reconstruct part of the citation graph of astronomy papers from their figures and captions alone?The dataset comprises over 100K figure-and-caption pairs drawn from recent open-access astronomy papers.TASKMulti-class, single-label classification. Each input is a pair of objects: two figures, a figure and a caption, or two captions. The relation is symmetric, and each pair has exactly one label:- same figure: the two objects come from the same scientific figure (figure-caption pairs only)- same paper: the two objects come from the same paper (same DOI)- related papers: one object's paper cites the other's- unrelated papers: none of the aboveA note on scope: AstroCLIMB is meant as a benchmark for multimodal models rather than an end in itself. Participants are not expected to train large models from scratch for it; computing basic statistics or folding it into a larger multimodal training pipeline is very much in keeping with the intent.DATATwo versions of the same dataset are available:- Full dataset (Hugging Face): over 94K rows, each with a figure, its caption, and metadata (source DOI, title, authors, cited and citing DOIs) describing an astronomy citation graph as an adjacency list. Pairs are not enumerated; you generate them from the adjacency list.  https://huggingface.co/datasets/adsabs/AstroCLIMB- Evaluation dataset (Kaggle): 10K enumerated pairs each in the train and test splits, with labels. Many more pairs can be generated from the full dataset.  https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/astroclimb/overviewIn the Kaggle data, some objects are English-language strings, and others are images encoded as strings; Kaggle provides a helper notebook to decode them into images.EVALUATIONKaggle evaluates systems using macro-F1 across the four classes. Submissions are CSV files with per-class indicators; a sample submission is available on the competition page.HOW TO PARTICIPATE1. Register and join the competition on Kaggle to access the data and score submissions:   https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/astroclimb/overview2. Optionally, write up your system description as a paper using the ACL LaTeX template   (https://github.com/acl-org/acl-style-files) and submit it via OpenReview:   https://openreview.net/group?id=aclweb.org/AACL-IJCNLP/2026/Workshop/WASPSystem description papers undergo light peer review and, if accepted, are published in the WASP 2026 proceedings in the ACL Anthology. postings.conferenceName: Social Media and Health - Well-being: Physical and Mental
postings.conferenceText: The relationship between social media and human well-being is one of the most urgent questions in health communication today. We are now accepting submissions for the Well-Being: Physical and Mental section of Social Media in Culture & Society, an Oxford Intersections series published by Oxford University Press.Social media plays a complex role in shaping physical and mental well-being, offering opportunities for connection, support, and health awareness while also introducing risks such as misinformation, cyberbullying, and addictive behaviours. This section explores how platform design, data practices, and emerging technologies like AI influence user well-being, highlighting tensions between empowerment and harm alongside key issues of privacy, autonomy, and ethical governance. We welcome rigorous, interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of health communication, digital media, and well-being — including topics such as:→ Social connectivity: balancing community benefits and cyber risks → Cyberbullying in the digital age: identification, prevention, and support → The weight of online personas: pressures and expectations → Cognitive impact of digital overload and constant content consumption → Strategies for digital detox and mental well-being → Positive digital environments: building safe and supportive communities → The role of social media in mental health awareness and advocacy → Datafication of well-beingWe welcome original research across theoretical, quantitative, qualitative, and computational social science approaches. Health communication scholars are especially encouraged to submit. We also welcome submissions from doctoral candidates in the final stages of their dissertation.Please contact eeikey@ucsd.edu with questions or abstract submissions.

postings.conferenceName: 3rd SOCAISA WORKSHOP
postings.conferenceText: Bridging SOC, AI & IoTSOCAISA explores the convergence of Service-Oriented Computing, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet of Things — addressing the critical challenges of interoperability and scalability in the design of intelligent, interconnected systems.Interoperability ChallengesIn the context of SOC and IoT, interoperability remains a fundamental challenge due to the diverse nature of devices, protocols, and service interfaces. AI techniques offer promising solutions by enabling systems to autonomously understand and adapt to varying data formats and communication protocols. Semantic technologies and NLP can standardize service descriptions, enhancing discovery and composition across heterogeneous environments.Scalability SolutionsAs IoT deployments expand exponentially, generating massive data volumes, SOC frameworks must efficiently process and manage them at scale. AI-driven approaches — edge computing, distributed learning, federated architectures — enable decentralized decision-making, reducing latency and enhancing scalability. Predictive analytics and dynamic resource allocation allow SOC architectures to adapt to real-time demand.AI as a Convergence EngineArtificial Intelligence is no longer a standalone layer: it acts as the convergence engine that makes SOC and IoT systems adaptive, context-aware, and self-healing. From LLMs as service orchestrators to federated learning across IoT nodes, AI fundamentally reshapes how services are discovered, composed, and governed.Research & PracticeSOCAISA brings together researchers and practitioners from three communities to produce cross-disciplinary insights, establish a shared vocabulary, and define a forward-looking research agenda. The workshop covers the full spectrum — from formal models and middleware design to real-world deployments and benchmarking frameworks.Research Focus AreasThe workshop welcomes contributions across the following themes, without being limited to them.AI & ServicesAI Integration in Service-Oriented Systems AI-Driven Service Orchestration and Composition AI-Enhanced Service Discovery and Recommendation AI-Based SLA Management AI-Driven Adaptive and Self-Healing Systems AI for Quality of Service (QoS) Optimization AI-Enabled Security and Privacy in SOC Intent-Based Service ComputingLLMs & Generative AILLMs as Service Orchestrators in IoT Environments Generative AI for Automated Service Configuration Small Language Models (SLMs) for Resource-Constrained IoT Explainable AI (XAI) for Trustworthy Service SystemsIoT & Edge ComputingAI for IoT and Edge Computing Integration Context-Aware AI Technologies for Services and IoT Edge-Cloud Continuum Architectures for Intelligent IoT Distributed LLM Inference at the Edge AI-Enabled Sustainable IoT SolutionsInteroperability & SemanticsSemantic-Based IoT Solutions for Interoperability Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving IoT ServicesData, Cloud & InfrastructureBig Data Management in Service-Oriented IoT Microservices and Serverless Architectures for Scalable IoT Carbon-Aware Service Scheduling in IoT InfrastructuresEmerging ParadigmsDigital Twin Frameworks for IoT Service Management Blockchain for Decentralized Trust and SLA Enforcement AI-Driven SOC for Smart Health, Smart Cities & Industry 4.0Submission & PublicationAuthors are invited to submit original, unpublished research contributions.Format RequirementsFull papers must not exceed 12 pages (including references and appendices), formatted according to the Springer LNCS template.Papers must be submitted as PDF files via the EasyChair platform. If you encounter any issue during submission, contact us at Karim.guennoun@ehtp.ac.ma.Each submission will be reviewed by at least three members of the international program committee, evaluated on originality, significance, technical soundness, and clarity.PublicationAll accepted papers will be published in the workshop proceedings as part of the Lecture Notes in Computer Science (LNCS) series by Springer.At least one author of each accepted paper must register and present at the workshop. Registration follows the terms of the main ICSOC 2026 conference.

postings.conferenceText: COLING 2027: First Call for Papers Website: https://2027.coling-iccl.org/The 32nd International Conference on Computational Linguistics (COLING 2027) will take place in Macau, China, May 9-14 2027. COLING 2027 invites the submission of long and short papers featuring substantial, original, and unpublished research in all aspects of computational linguistics and natural language processing. Relevant topics include, but are not limited to, the following areas:    Benchmarking and Evaluation    Computational Cognitive Modeling and Psycholinguistics    Computational Social Science and Sociolinguistics    Cross-lingual and Multilingual NLP (including Machine Translation)    Dialogue and Interactive Systems    NLP for Digital Humanities and Cultural Analytics    Discourse and Pragmatics    Ethics, Bias, Fairness, Alignment and Security    Human-AI Interaction and Social Impact of AI systems (including User Studies)    Information Extraction and Retrieval     Interpretability and Analysis of NLP Models     Knowledge-based NLP and Reasoning     Language Acquisition, Learning and Evolution    Language Diversity and NLP for Low-resourced/Less-studied Languages    Language Modeling, including Novel Architectures    Language Resources    Linguistic Theories and Language Modeling for Linguistic Insights    Machine Learning, including Resource-efficiency and Explainability    Agent-based LLM systems     Morphology and Syntax: Segmentation, Tagging, Chunking and Parsing    Multimodality and Language Grounding to Vision, Robotics and Beyond    Natural Language Generation, Summarization and Simplification    NLP and LLM Applications    Phonology and Speech: Recognition, Synthesis, Spoken Language Modeling    Semantics: Lexical and Sentence-Level    Sentiment Analysis, Opinion and Argument Mining, Offensive Language DetectionCOLING 2027 will also feature a special theme track devoted to uses of NLP/LLMs in service of linguistic research, with a particular focus on linguistic diversity. A more detailed description of the special theme will be distributed in mid-August.Submission DetailsAll papers must be submitted through ACL Rolling Review (ARR). The latest possible time to submit is the ARR 2026 October cycle, but papers that have already received reviews and a meta-review from ARR from earlier cycles can also be committed to COLING 2027. Please note that the October ARR cycle is shared between COLING 2027 and NAACL 2027 and that authors will be able to choose which conference they want to commit their paper to (only) after the meta-reviews have been released. COLING 2027 invites the submission of long papers of up to eight (8) pages and short papers of up to four (4) pages. These page limits only apply to the main body of the paper. At the end of the paper (after the conclusion but before the references) papers need to include a mandatory section discussing the limitations of the work and, optionally, a section discussing ethical considerations. Papers can include unlimited pages of references and an unlimited appendix. Authors should follow the general instructions for COLING 2027 proceedings, which will be published on the conference website together with submission templates.Important Dates    ARR submission deadline (long & short papers): October 12, 2026    Commitment after meta-reviews: December 23, 2026    Notification of acceptance: February 10, 2027    Main Conference: May 9–14, 2027General Chairs    Katrin Erk, University of Massachusetts Amherst    Chengqing Zong, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of SciencesProgram Chairs    Minlie Huang, Tsinghua University    Joakim Nivre, Uppsala University    Alexis Palmer, University of Colorado Boulder    Sina Zarrieß, University of BielefeldFor questions about submissions: coling2027-pcchairs@googlegroups.com

postings.conferenceName: ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing - Cyber-Physical Systems Track
postings.conferenceText: =========================================================================                    CALL FOR PAPERS The 42nd ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing (SAC 2027)            Cyber-Physical Systems Track       Gwangju, South Korea, April 5-9, 2027  https://conference.cs.cityu.edu.hk/saccps/2027/=========================================================================-------------------------------------------------------------------------Important Dates-------------------------------------------------------------------------Submission of regular papers                - October 2, 2026 (EST)Notification of paper acceptance/rejection  - November 13, 2026Camera-ready copies of accepted papers      - November 28, 2026Author registration due date                - December 5, 2026-------------------------------------------------------------------------Objectives and Scope-------------------------------------------------------------------------The purpose of the Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) track is to foster multidisciplinary exchange on the emerging challenges and innovations shaping the next generation of CPS. CPS are engineered systems whose operations are monitored, coordinated, controlled, and integrated by a computing and communication core embedded in all types of objects and structures in the physical environment. CPS has emerged as a unifying name for systems where the cyber parts, i.e., the computing and communication components, and the physical parts are tightly integrated, both at the design time and during operation. Such systems use computations and communication deeply embedded in and interacting with physical processes to add new capabilities to physical systems. Such systems must be operated safely, dependably, securely, efficiently and in real-time. CPS span diverse application domains that underpin critical social infrastructure, including transportation, healthcare, energy, manufacturing, aerospace, and robotics. Therefore, advances in this field will have significant technical, economic and societal impacts in the near future. However, the vision of CPS faces core multidisciplinary research challenges, as relevant technologies span diverse areas of science and engineering. Thus, there is an emerging consensus that new methodologies and tools are urgently needed to support CPS.-------------------------------------------------------------------------Topics of interest-------------------------------------------------------------------------* Ubiquitous and pervasive computing with CPS* Mobile computing and devices for CPS* Wearable CPS and applications* Design automation and tool chains for CPS* Networking and communication for CPS applications* Cloud computing and distributed systems for CPS* Intermittent and sustainable computing for CPS* Real-time CPS* Control of CPS* Safety and dependability for CPS* Security and privacy of CPS* Resilient and robust systems design for CPS* Machine learning for CPS* Simulation and experimental prototypes of CPS-------------------------------------------------------------------------Paper submission and acceptance-------------------------------------------------------------------------To submit a paper, please follow the URL:https://easychair.org/my/conference?conf=sac2027Authors are invited to submit original, unpublished research and application papers to this track. Full papers are limited to 8 pages, with up to 2 additional pages permitted for an extra charge. Papers must follow the ACM SAC template. To facilitate double-blind review, author names and addresses must be omitted, and self-references should be written in the third person. Concurrent submissions to other conferences or journals are not permitted and will be automatically rejected. Full submission guidelines, formatting requirements, and access to the submission portal are available on the ACM SAC 2027 website:https://www.sigapp.org/sac/sac2027Paper registration and presentation by an author or proxy at ACM SAC are required for inclusion in the conference proceedings and ACM Digital Library. Registered papers that are not presented will be excluded from the ACM Digital Library.-------------------------------------------------------------------------CPS Track Chairs-------------------------------------------------------------------------Hashan Roshantha Mendis (Academia Sinica, Taiwan)Jingtong Hu (University of Pittsburgh, USA)Pi-Cheng Hsiu (Academia Sinica, Taiwan)For further information on SAC 2027 CPS track, please contact the track chair Rosh Mendis: rosh.mendis@citi.sinica.edu.tw

postings.conferenceName: Spatio-Temporal Data Management and Analysis for Knowledge Discovery Workshop
postings.conferenceText: Call for Papers - STMA4KD Workshop Spatio-Temporal Data Management and Analysis for Knowledge Discovery Workshop@ CIKM 2026 - Rome, Italy - November 8, 2026 (Workshop Day)https://gt-gast.irisa.fr/stm4kd/Abstract: STMA4KD invites submissions on the management and analysis of spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal data for knowledge discovery. The workshop will provide an international forum for researchers and practitioners in data management, knowledge discovery, information retrieval, machine learning, and application domains to exchange methods, systems, datasets, benchmarks, and emerging research questions. The program will combine peer-reviewed contributions with interactive presentations and discussion, and may include an invited talk or panel.Organising Committee:    Clément Iphar, CRC / Mines Paris - PSL (Sophia Antipolis, France)    Aurélie Leborgne, ICube / University of Strasbourg (Strasbourg, France)    Nida Meddouri, LRE / EPITA (Paris, France)    Loïc Salmon, ISEA / University of New Caledonia (Nouméa, New Caledonia)    Juba Agoun, ERIC Research Unit / Université Lumière Lyon 2 (Lyon, France)    Assaad Zeghina, LATMOS (UVSQ / Sorbonne University) / Inria (Paris, France)    Nazha Selmaoui, ISEA / University of New Caledonia (Nouméa, New Caledonia)Description: Spatial and temporal information has become a first-class concern in knowledge and information management. Data associated with time and location arise in web and open data, sensor infrastructures, multimodal analytics, document collections, mobility systems, Earth observation, environmental monitoring, healthcare trajectories, maritime intelligence, and public-sector platforms. STMA4KD adopts a broad view of such data: submissions may analyze explicitly georeferenced or timestamped data, or extract spatial and temporal knowledge from complex sources such as text, images, video, maps, and multimodal streams. Relevant challenges span acquisition, integration, representation, storage, querying, analysis, visualization, and dissemination in batch, streaming, centralized, distributed, or federated settings.Despite rapid advances in time-series analysis, trajectory mining, geo-temporal learning, and sensor analytics, research remains fragmented across domains. Many communities nevertheless face shared challenges, including heterogeneous data integration, scalability, uncertainty, privacy, data quality, explainability, robust evaluation, and reproducibility. STMA4KD is intended as a cross-disciplinary venue in which these common bottlenecks can be examined through methods, systems, resources, and applications.Objectives: The workshop aims to bring together researchers and practitioners from academia, industry, and the public sector who address spatial and temporal information throughout the data lifecycle. It seeks to connect data management, knowledge discovery, information retrieval, machine learning, and application communities; encourage exchange between methodological and domain-driven research; identify reusable approaches, benchmarks, datasets, and evaluation protocols; and formulate shared research priorities and open problems. STMA4KD builds on the GAST workshop series while extending its scope to a broader international CIKM audience.Workshop Topics (non-exhaustive list): We welcome contributions on needs, challenges, tools, techniques, methods, algorithms, systems, and resources involving:    Temporal data: time series, sequences, event data, temporal graphs, longitudinal records, etc...    Spatial data: geospatial databases, maps, remote-sensing imagery, geomatics, maritime data, etc.;    Spatio-temporal data: trajectories, mobility traces, sensor networks, biological and medical data, moving objects, video, satellite image sequences, territorial data, etc.;    Textual and multimodal sources containing or implying spatial and temporal information;    Streaming and real-time data with spatial and/or temporal dimensions;    Federated, privacy-sensitive, or geographically distributed spatial and temporal data.The following research questions and topics are particularly welcome:    Data acquisition, cleaning, quality assessment, integration, and provenance for spatial and temporal data;    Modeling, representation, indexing, querying, storage, and scalable management of spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal information;    Heterogeneous, multidimensional, multiscale, multimodal, and semantic geo-temporal data integration;    Machine learning, deep learning, graph-based learning, symbolic AI, and hybrid methods for spatial and temporal data;    Pattern, rule, sequence, trajectory, and event discovery, including classification, prediction, clustering, and anomaly detection;    Streaming analytics and real-time processing for trajectories, sensors, and event data;    Uncertainty-aware, robust, and quality-conscious analysis and management;    Privacy, anonymity, security, federated learning, and distributed processing for geographically dispersed data;    Explainability, interpretability, visualization, and human-centered interaction for spatial and temporal models;    Benchmarks, datasets, evaluation protocols, reproducibility, open science, and shared resources.Contributions may address these questions conceptually, methodologically, systemically, or through applications in transportation and mobility, Earth observation, environmental monitoring, maritime systems, healthcare, public safety, digital humanities, industry, and the public sector. Methods, models, tools, datasets, and evaluation frameworks that transfer across application domains are particularly encouraged. Important Dates (all deadlines are at 11:59 PM AoE):- Paper submission deadline: August 24, 2026- Notification of acceptance: September 23, 2026- Workshop: November 8, 2026Instructions for Authors: Authors are invited to submit original work that has not been previously published and is not simultaneously under review elsewhere. Three submission formats are accepted: poster/extended abstracts of up to 2 pages; short papers of up to 4-6 pages; and full papers of 8-10 pages. Full papers should report mature methodological, system, or applied contributions. Short papers may present work in progress, datasets, benchmark proposals, reproducibility studies, or focused empirical findings. Poster/extended abstracts may describe emerging ideas, early-stage results, systems, or industry use cases.Submissions must be written in English, prepared in PDF using the ACM two-column "sigconf" proceedings template (https://www.acm.org/publications/proceedings-template).Submission: All submissions must be submitted electronically through the Microsoft CMT platform following this link: https://cmt3.research.microsoft.com/STMAKD2026/ Workshop papers will not be included in the ACM conference proceedings. We will publish proceedings for our workshop.Each submission will receive at least two reviews. The evaluation criteria are:    Relevance of the scientific content to the scope and themes of STMA4KD;    Originality, significance, and potential impact of the contribution;    Scientific and technical quality, including methodological soundness and appropriate evaluation;    Clarity of presentation and accessibility to a multidisciplinary audience;    Potential to stimulate constructive scientific discussion and contribute to shared research priorities.At least one author of each accepted contribution must register for CIKM 2026 and present the work on site in Rome, Italy. Registration fees and procedures will be available on the CIKM 2026 website: https://cikm2026.diag.uniroma1.it/.Acknowledgement : "The Microsoft CMT service was used for managing the peer-reviewing process for this conference. This service was provided for free by Microsoft and they bore all expenses, including costs for Azure cloud services as well as for software development and support." Contact: clement.iphar@minesparis.psl.eu and nida.meddouri@epita.fr

The goal of the International Conference on Big Data and Smart Computing (BigComp), initiated by KIISE (Korean Institute of Information Scientists and Engineers), is to provide an international forum for exchanging ideas and information on current studies, challenges, research results, system developments, and practical experiences in these emerging fields among researchers, developers, and users from academia, business and industry. Following the successes of the previous BigComp conferences in Bangkok, Thailand (2014), Jeju, Korea (2015), Hong Kong, China (2016), Jeju, Korea (2017), Shanghai, China (2018), Kyoto, Japan (2019), Busan, Korea (2020), Jeju, Korea (2021), Daegu, Korea (2022), Jeju, Korea (2023), Bangkok, Thailand (2024), Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia (2025), Guangzhou, China (2026), the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Big Data and Smart Computing (IEEE BigComp 2027) will be held in Fukuoka, Japan. The conference is co-sponsored by IEEE and KIISE. postings.conferenceText: The rapid growth of IoT systems across smart homes, healthcare, industry, transportation, and smart cities has created major challenges in security and privacy. IoT devices often operate with limited computation, weak authentication, heterogeneous communication protocols, and continuous data collection, making them vulnerable to attacks and privacy leakage. This workshop will bring together researchers and practitioners to discuss practical, scalable, and trustworthy approaches for securing IoT ecosystems while protecting user and device privacy.The workshop will focus on both theoretical and applied research related to IoT security and privacy. It will provide a forum for new ideas, system designs, experimental results, and real-world deployments. The workshop is intended to attract contributions from academia, industry, and government stakeholders working on secure connected systems. We invite the submission of original papers on all topics related to Intelligent Systems for Cybersecurity, with special interest in but not limited to:    Lightweight authentication and authorization for IoT devices.    Secure communication protocols for constrained devices.    Privacy-preserving data collection, sharing, and analytics.    Trust management and identity management in IoT ecosystems.    Secure edge computing and cloud-IoT architectures.    Intrusion detection and anomaly detection for IoT networks.    Blockchain and distributed ledger technologies for IoT security.    Secure firmware updates, device lifecycle protection, and supply-chain security.    Access control and data governance in smart environments.    Security and privacy in smart healthcare, smart homes, and smart cities.    Adversarial machine learning and AI-driven attacks on IoT systems.    Federated learning and privacy-preserving intelligence for IoT.    Legal, ethical, and regulatory aspects of IoT privacy.    Security and Privacy in the Internet of Battlefield Things (IoBT).    Security and Privacy in the Medical Internet of Things (MIoT), Internet of postings.conferenceName: ECHO: The 1st International Workshop on Edge-Cloud-HPC Operational Continuum at SC '26
postings.conferenceText: # Important DatesPaper submission deadline: August 15, 2026 (AoE)Author notification: September 4, 2026Camera-ready deadline, with AD/AE: September 25, 2026 (AoE)# About the WorkshopThe ECHO workshop brings together researchers and practitioners across edge systems, cloud platforms, and high-performance computing (HPC) to formulate and advance a shared research agenda. In this workshop, we explore how HPC, edge, and cloud ecosystems can mutually advance physically dispersed, field-to-cloud, geo-distributed computing pipelines, especially where mission-critical field operations demand robust edge capabilities—and identify how system architectures must adapt to thrive across this continuum.System design for modern workloads is end-to-end, e.g., driven by the sheer volume and rate of distributed data that can exceed the capability of on-scene devices. At the same time, high-fidelity data is continuously generated and acquired at the edge by bandwidth-hungry sources, such as scientific instruments, smart manufacturing arrays, and autonomous vehicle fleets. To satisfy strict real-time latency budgets and overcome intermittent network constraints, this raw data must be filtered, compressed, and partially processed near the sensors—often through in-situ feature extraction or low-latency AI inference. Only the highest-value signals and distilled datasets are then transmitted to the cloud, where they are aggregated to fuel resource-intensive tasks like massive-scale deep learning, digital twin simulations, and continuous model refinement.Stewardship throughout the entire data lifecycle—encompassing data governance, data quality assurance, and policy-driven oversight—has shifted beyond a narrow focus on centralized task processing. Today, it demands sophisticated workflow orchestration and data management across a computing continuum that spans sensors, edge devices, and cloud platforms. At the same time, these use cases are highly performance-critical. They increasingly require capabilities long associated with HPC: efficient parallel execution, high-throughput data movement, high-performance I/O, accelerator utilization, topology-aware communication, and rigorous performance engineering.# Workshop FormatECHO will be held as a half-day workshop on the morning of Nov. 20, 2026 (Friday), in conjunction with SC '26 in Chicago, IL. The program combines featured talks that set context, peer-reviewed paper and lightning sessions, a multi-stakeholder panel spanning academia, industry, and national labs, and interactive breakouts for structured ideation and report-backs.The mix is intentional: guided breakouts drive problem formulation, lightning talks and feedback-oriented Q&A socialize early-stage and work-in-progress results, and mixed panels and breakout groups build bridges across the HPC, edge, distributed-systems, networking, and AI-infrastructure communities.

postings.conferenceName: Narrative Atoms: The Persistence and Transformation of Fundamental Story Units in Culture
postings.conferenceText: Kraków, Faculty of Management and Social Communication, Jagiellonian University🌐 Conference languages: Polish and EnglishConference format: hybrid (on-site and online)International participants are welcome to join the conference remotely.About the ConferenceThe conference aims to explore elementary narrative structures that organize cultural experience and contribute to the construction of meaning—from oral traditions to contemporary forms of digital communication.At the center of discussion are “narrative atoms”, understood as minimal, repeatable matrices of meaning-making that function across different media and historical contexts.Proposed Areas of Inquiry1. Ontology and Theory of “Narrative Atoms”•	Epistemological status of basic narrative structures: universal or historically variable?•	Persistence of archetypal patterns despite technological and media change•	Elementary narrative structures as models of knowledge organization and complexity reduction•	Hybridization and recontextualization of traditional patterns in late modern culture•	Relationships between elementary and complex narrative systems•	Basic structures within extended narratives (novel, film, series, historiography)•	Historical models of meaning-making as configurations of recurring patterns2. Media and Digital Transformations•	Relations between orality, literacy, and digitality: continuity and rupture•	Transformations of pre-literate narrative patterns in digital environments (memes, games, fan fiction, social media)•	Elementary narrative units in cybertext, virtual literature, and immersive forms•	Narrative patterns in visual culture: art, film, series, comics, audiovisual media•	Adaptations of myth, saga, and legend in film, TV series, and games as forms of media translocation3. Social and Cultural Functions•	Social and identity-related functions of narrative patterns in contemporary digital culture•	Elementary structures as carriers of collective memory and cultural transmission•	Archetypal forms in historical narratives and historiography•	Narrative patterns in folk and popular culture•	Use of basic narrative structures in advertising, propaganda, and political communication•	Short forms (jokes, proverbs, aphorisms) as tools for negotiating norms and symbolic orders📩 Abstract submission deadline: 31 July 2026👉 Submission form: Conference Registration Form – Wypełnij formularz💰 Conference fee: 500 PLN / 150 EUR

postings.conferenceName: The 6th Annual FHE.org Conference on Fully Homomorphic Encryption
postings.conferenceText: The 6th Annual FHE.org Conference on Fully Homomorphic Encryption is co-located with Real World Crypto 2027 in Seattle, Washington, on April 4th 2027.-- Motivation and scope --The FHE.org conference is the premier forum gathering researchers, technologists and practitioners working on the design, development, deployment, validation, and application of fully homomorphic encryption (FHE).Nearly two decades have passed since Gentry's 2009 construction showed that FHE was possible, transforming a thirty-year open problem into a living research field. The years since have delivered orders-of-magnitude improvements in performance, a rich family of schemes suited to different computational models, and a growing ecosystem of open-source libraries, compilers, and hardware accelerators. That research momentum continues today, with a rich future of exploration and transition to practice.As for previous editions, FHE.org 2027 welcomes talks and posters that advance the theoretical and algorithmic foundations of the field. This could include, for example, novel algorithms for faster homomorphic evaluation; cryptanalysis, attacks and countermeasures; precision, accuracy and noise analysis; or security notions for FHE.This year, however, we place particular emphasis on the transition from possibility to practice. Governments and industry are moving FHE out of the laboratory and into procurement decisions, pilot deployments, and standards processes. This shift raises questions the FHE.org community is uniquely positioned to answer, including:* What are the emerging industry-relevant and industry-scale use cases for FHE?  * What does production readiness mean for encrypted computation?   * How do we transform FHE from a domain where only a few hundred experts worldwide can write and debug real applications to an everyday programming domain accessible to the 40 million or so programmers in the world?  * How do we benchmark and compare real FHE systems?   * How do we pragmatically deploy the acceleration needed to make FHE fast enough for a first generation of deployed applications?  * Where do deployments succeed, and where and why do they stall?   * What are the remaining gaps in FHE as a full solution within a privacy-preserving system, and how do we practically address them?The 2027 FHE.org Program Committee is particularly seeking talks and posters that speak to these questions. The [FHE.org](http://fhe.org) 2027 conference will emphasise FHE as an engineering discipline and a deployable technology, alongside the foundational work that continues to expand what is possible.-- Call for contributed talks and posters --Authors are invited to submit proposals for presentation as a talk or poster using the submission form located at https://easychair.org/conferences/?conf=fheorg2027. Submissions must be in PDF format and written in English and should be in the form of an extended abstract of 2 to 4 pages (not including references). Whether the proposal is for a talk or poster should be clearly indicated in the submission. Submission implies the willingness of at least one of the authors to register and present the contribution in person at the conference venue. Every year, we receive many proposals for presentations of great quality, and it is not always possible to accept all of them as talks. A submission for a talk may instead be accepted as a poster.FHE.org follows the spirit of the Real World Cryptography conference, and so submissions are single-blind. All submissions will be refereed by the program committee who will be asked to consider both (1) the relevance of the submission to the goals of the conference and (2), in the case of a talk proposal, the quality of the presentation. For a proposal for a talk, the author who will present the talk should be identified.The final program will consist of invited talks, contributed talks, and a poster session. There are no published proceedings at FHE.org. This means that both invited and contributed talks may appear at other conferences with proceedings. Authors of accepted abstracts can choose to have a link to a preprint on the conference webpage.-- Important dates --* Submission deadline: November 1, 2026 (23:59 AoE time)  * Notification: December 18, 2026  * Conference date: April 4, 2027

postings.conferenceName: 10th International Symposium on Model-Based Safety Assessment
postings.conferenceText: IMBSA 2027 – Call for PapersInternational Symposium on Model-Based Safety and AssessmentModern safety-critical systems are changing rapidly. They increasingly combine physical components, complex software, connected services, autonomous behaviour and artificial intelligence. Machine learning, foundation models and intelligent agents are moving from experimental technologies into systems whose behaviour can have real consequences for people, infrastructure and society.At the same time, the fundamental challenge remains unchanged: how can we understand, predict and assure the behaviour of complex systems before failures occur?IMBSA brings together researchers, practitioners, tool developers and industry working on model-based and automated approaches to safety, dependability and assurance. The symposium provides a forum where advances in modelling, formal analysis, probabilistic reasoning, system engineering and safety assurance meet emerging developments in AI, autonomy and digital engineering.IMBSA 2027 invites contributions that advance the state of the art, demonstrate methods on realistic systems, report lessons from industrial practice, or challenge the community with important new problems.We particularly encourage work that connects established strengths of model-based safety engineering with the new assurance challenges created by increasingly complex, autonomous, adaptive and AI-enabled systems.A conference connecting research, technology and practiceIMBSA is intended not simply as a venue for presenting papers, but as a meeting place for the model-based safety and assurance community.The symposium brings together:•	Scientific research, presenting new theories, methods and evidence;•	Industrial experience, showing how safety and assurance methods perform on real systems and where important challenges remain;•	Tools and demonstrations, allowing participants to experience new technologies rather than merely read about them;•	Emerging ideas, creating space for discussion of new system classes, new risks and new approaches to assurance.This interaction is particularly important today. Safety engineering must increasingly deal with systems that are interconnected, software-intensive, data-driven, adaptive and capable of making autonomous decisions. Traditional analysis remains essential, but it must evolve to address systems whose behaviour may change during operation and whose failure mechanisms cannot always be captured entirely at design time.IMBSA 2027 seeks work that helps shape that evolution.Topics of InterestWe welcome contributions on all aspects of model-based safety, dependability and assurance, including (but not limited to) the following broad themes.Model-Based Safety and DependabilityModel-based safety assessment and analysis; dependability modelling; failure and fault propagation; causal and probabilistic analysis; dynamic risk assessment; reliability, availability, maintainability and resilience; model-driven safety engineering.System Engineering, Architecture and Digital EngineeringSafety-aware architectures; integration of MBSE and safety engineering; cyber-physical and software-intensive systems; systems of systems; digital twins; simulation and co-simulation; model interoperability; engineering lifecycle integration.AI, Autonomy and Intelligent SystemsSafety and assurance of machine learning, generative AI, foundation models and AI agents; autonomous and adaptive systems; intelligent robotics; multi-agent systems; human–AI teaming; uncertainty and confidence assessment; explainability; runtime monitoring and assurance; AI-assisted safety engineering.Verification, Validation and Safety AssuranceFormal methods; model checking; specification and verification of safety requirements; simulation- and scenario-based verification; testing and fault injection; safety and assurance cases; continuous and runtime assurance; evidence generation; certification, standards and regulatory compliance.Safety, Security and ResilienceIntegrated safety and cybersecurity analysis; threat, hazard and risk modelling; adversarial behaviour; fault and attack propagation; resilience of interconnected and AI-enabled systems; trustworthy operation under uncertainty.Tools, Automation and Industrial ApplicationsSafety analysis tools and toolchains; automated generation and analysis of safety models; knowledge-based and data-driven approaches; benchmarks and datasets; industrial case studies and deployment experience across domains including aerospace, automotive, transport, robotics, energy, manufacturing, healthcare, maritime systems, critical infrastructure and other safety-critical applications.This list is deliberately broad. We particularly welcome submissions that cross traditional boundaries. For example, by combining model-based and data-driven techniques, connecting design-time analysis with runtime assurance, or applying established safety concepts to emerging forms of autonomy and AI.Types of ContributionsIMBSA 2027 solicits Regular Papers and Short Papers.Regular PapersRegular papers should present significant and original theoretical, methodological or practical results relevant to the model-based safety and assurance community and clearly explain their contribution beyond the state of the art.Suitable contributions include:•	Research papers presenting new theories, methodologies or technologies;•	Industrial and case-study papers demonstrating application at realistic or industrial scale;•	Tool papers presenting significant safety or assurance tools, platforms and integrated toolchains;•	Industrial experience papers describing deployment, evaluation, challenges and lessons learned;•	AI safety and assurance papers addressing the modelling, analysis, verification and assurance of AI-enabled, autonomous or intelligent systems.Regular papers should be 12–15 pages, including references and appendices, and will normally be presented orally at the symposium.Short PapersShort papers provide a more flexible route for bringing new ideas, emerging research, early results and practical technologies to the IMBSA community.They may present:•	promising research directions or challenging open problems;•	preliminary methods and results;•	industrial applications and experience;•	new tools and demonstrations;•	datasets and benchmarks;•	emerging safety and assurance concepts;•	provocative positions that can stimulate discussion within the community.Short papers should be 4–6 pages and may be presented orally or as a poster or demonstration, at the discretion of the Program Committee.Authors of accepted tool and demonstration papers will have the opportunity to present their technology live during an interactive conference session.Why Submit to IMBSA 2027?The challenges facing safety engineering increasingly sit between disciplines. A safety engineer may need to understand machine learning; an AI researcher may need to reason about hazards and assurance; a system architect may need models that remain connected to operational evidence; and industry needs methods that can move beyond laboratory demonstrations into credible engineering practice.IMBSA 2027 aims to bring these communities together.We therefore particularly encourage submissions that:•	demonstrate genuinely new approaches to difficult safety and dependability problems;•	connect models to evidence from real systems;•	bridge research and industrial application;•	integrate methods that have traditionally been studied separately;•	make safety analysis more automated, scalable or usable;•	address the assurance of AI-enabled and autonomous systems without abandoning rigorous engineering foundations;•	identify important problems for which current methods are simply not good enough.Whether your contribution develops a new theory, analyses a complex industrial system, introduces a practical tool, tests an existing method under realistic conditions, or opens an important new research direction, we would like IMBSA 2027 to be the place where that work is discussed.Submission and PublicationRegular and short papers must be prepared using the Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science (LNCS) templates.Submissions should be made through the IMBSA 2027 EasyChair system:https://easychair.org/my/conference?conf=imbsa2027All submissions will undergo full review by the Program Committee.Regular contributions are planned for publication in the Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science (LNCS)proceedings.At least one author of each accepted paper must register for and participate in the conference for the paper to be included in the proceedings.Authors should consult the Important Dates section of the IMBSA 2027 website for the current deadlines for abstract submission, full paper submission, notification and camera-ready papers.________________________________________Join the IMBSA community in 2027As engineered systems acquire greater complexity, connectivity, intelligence and autonomy, assuring their behaviour is becoming both more difficult and more important.IMBSA 2027 invites the safety, dependability, systems engineering and AI communities to help define the methods by which these systems can be understood, assessed and ultimately trusted.We look forward to your contributions.Website: https://cyprusconferences.org/imbsa2027/

Encompassing a spectrum from foundational theoryto practical implementation, it spans systems of all scales—from smallconfigurations to the largest infrastructures. PDP addresses fundamentalcomputational challenges alongside robust applications and delves intoarchitecture, compiler, language, interface design and deployment,tools, support infrastructures, and performance optimization.Parallel, Distributed, and Network-Based Processing fields have evolvedsignificantly, marked by the emergence of novel architectures andgroundbreaking applications. Artificial intelligence (AI) has become amajor application area, leveraging parallel and distributed technologiesto enhance computational efficiency and enable sophisticated AI models.This progress emphasizes the dynamic fusion of parallel and distributedtechnologies with other rapidly advancing domains. In evaluating thesecutting-edge developments, it is imperative to highlight the latestresearch achievements in established areas of parallel and distributedcomputing, drawing insights from both industrial and academicperspectives.PDP 2027 brings researchers and practitioners together in Barcelona topresent new work and discuss where the field is heading next. postings.conferenceName: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Foundation Models for the Brain and Body
postings.conferenceText: We are pleased to announce the second edition of the “Foundation Models for the Brain and Body” workshop at NeurIPS 2026 in Sydney, Australia.The workshop brings together researchers at the intersection of biosignals, neuroscience, machine learning, and embodied intelligence. We invite submissions of short papers on novel research in neuroscience, biosignal analysis, machine learning, and embodied AI, with a focus on foundation models and representation learning for neural, physiological, and behavioral data. We also invite interactive demo proposals showcasing novel methods, devices, systems, or applications.We broadly define biosignals as any temporal signal directly or indirectly generated by the brain or body. This includes neural recordings such as EEG, MEG, and multi-electrode arrays; physiological signals such as heart rate, respiration, and EMG; and behavioral signals such as pose, gaze, and movement. Submissions may focus on methods, applications, or theoretical insights that advance our understanding and modeling of neural, physiological, and behavioral signals in humans and animals. We particularly encourage work on scalable foundation models that generalize across tasks, subjects, modalities, or domains.Relevant topics include, but are not limited to:• Large-scale pretraining on neural or physiological signals• Scaling laws for biosignal foundation models• Brain-computer interfaces and neural decoding• Transfer learning across recording modalities• Cross-subject and cross-task generalization• Few-shot, zero-shot, and continual learning• Multimodal integration of biosignals• Wearable technology and real-world deployment• Modeling behavioral signals such as pose, gaze, and movement• Foundation models for movement, motor control, and EMG• Embodied intelligence and sensorimotor representation learning• Closed-loop and interactive systems, including BCI control and assistive robotics• Scaling techniques from robotics and control applied to biosignal modeling• Applications to health and clinical diagnosis• Interpretability of biosignal representations• Synthetic data generation and augmentation• Human-AI collaboration for signal interpretation and labeling• Open datasets, benchmarks, and model evaluation• Evaluation protocols and standardized benchmarks across modalities• Reproducibility and standardized reportingImportant Dates (AoE)• Paper Submission Deadline: September 4, 2026• Demo Submission Deadline: September 19, 2026• Paper Author Notification: September 29, 2026• Workshop Date: December 11 or 12, 2026, in Sydney, AustraliaStay tuned for announcements about our invited speakers, panelists, and workshop schedule.For submission details and more information, please visit: https://brainbodyfm-workshop.github.io/

postings.conferenceName: Real-Time Conversational Agents Workshop at NeurIPS 2026
postings.conferenceText: Real-Time Conversational Agents (RTCA) Workshop @ NeurIPS 2026Sydney, Australia — 11 or 12 December 2026Website: https://rtcaneurips26.github.io/Submission portal (OpenReview): https://openreview.net/group?id=NeurIPS.cc/2026/Workshop/RTCA*** Submission deadline: 29 August 2026 (Anywhere on Earth) ***We are pleased to share the Call for Papers and Demos for the inaugural Real-Time Conversational Agents (RTCA) Workshop, held in conjunction with NeurIPS 2026 in Sydney, Australia.OVERVIEWConversational AI has moved from text chat into the real world — voice modes, embodied avatars, and agents that share our screens and tools. To feel natural, these systems must operate in real time: streaming speech, video, and language while continuously listening, watching, and re-planning. This is fundamentally harder than offline generation — latency, turn-taking, backchannels, interruptions, and cross-modal alignment all become first-class problems that the offline-generation paradigm largely sidesteps. Recent progress on full-duplex speech-language models, real-time talking-head and avatar generation, low-latency speech synthesis, and streaming ASR shows that interactive multimodal agents are now technically feasible, but the field still lacks shared benchmarks, vocabulary, and methodology for interactional naturalness as distinct from per-utterance quality.RTCA brings together researchers across speech, vision, language, HCI, social-signal processing, and ML systems around three intertwined questions:Real-time generation under hard latency budgets — producing high-quality speech, video, and language in a streaming or full-duplex fashion.Naturalness in interaction — what makes an agent feel like a conversational partner (prosody, gaze, timing, grounding, expressivity, turn-taking).Evaluation of live systems — measuring naturalness, responsiveness, and conversational quality where standard offline metrics fall short.TOPICS OF INTEREST (non-exhaustive)Streaming/low-latency speech synthesis, ASR, and full-duplex audio-language modelsReal-time talking-head, avatar, and embodied video generation; lip-sync, gaze, expressivity under streamingStreaming language models; incremental and speculative decoding for dialogueTurn-taking, backchanneling, interruption handling, and floor managementMultimodal alignment under latency and partial-observation constraintsProsody, emotion, and paralinguistic generation in interactive settingsMemory, grounding, and tool use during live conversationEvaluation of naturalness: perceptual studies, turn-taking metrics, perceived latency, interactive Turing-style testsDatasets and benchmarks for interactive (not offline) evaluationEfficient inference, on-device deployment, and the systems-quality trade-offSafety, identity, and trust in real-time agents (deepfakes, persuasion, consent)Position papers, critiques of current evaluation practice, and reproducibility studies are also welcome.SUBMISSION TYPESFull papers (up to 8 pages) — original contributions; may be presented as posters and/or contributed talks.Short papers (up to 4 pages) — work in progress, focused contributions, or position papers.Demo papers (extended abstract or up to 2 pages) — required for the on-stage Conversational Agents Showcase.All submissions must use the NeurIPS 2026 style file and be formatted for double-blind review. Page limits exclude references and appendices. Papers must be submitted in PDF format via OpenReview. The workshop is non-archival; authors retain the right to publish elsewhere.IMPORTANT DATES (End of day, Anywhere on Earth)Call for papers opens: 18 July 2026Submission deadline (papers and demos): 29 August 2026Author notification: 29 September 2026Workshop date: 11 or 12 December 2026CONFIRMED INVITED SPEAKERSDimitris Samaras — Stony Brook University, USAEvonne Ng — Meta Reality Labs / UC Berkeley, USAORGANISERSNiki Foteinopoulou — Tavus, United KingdomAlessandro Conti — Tavus, ItalyJack Saunders — Tavus, United KingdomOya Celiktutan — King's College London, United KingdomCigdem Beyan — University of Verona, ItalyIoannis Patras — Queen Mary University of London, United KingdomCONTACTFor more information, visit https://rtcaneurips26.github.io/ or contact us at rtca-workshop@googlegroups.com.We look forward to your contributions.

postings.conferenceText: Welcome to AISEC4HSG’2026The first edition of the International Colloquium on Artificial Intelligence & Cybersecurity for Healthcare and Social Good (AISEC4HSG’2026) will be held on September 25–26, 2026 at the City of Innovation (CIM), Cadi Ayyad University, Marrakech, Morocco. The colloquium will be organized in a hybrid format, enabling participants to attend either in person or remotely.AISEC4HSG’2026 brings together PhD students, academic researchers, and industry professionals from diverse backgrounds to present and exchange innovative ideas, recent advances, and cutting-edge research in Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, and Intelligent Systems and Technologies for Healthcare and Social Good.The colloquium provides a premier interdisciplinary platform for researchers, practitioners, educators, and policymakers to discuss the latest innovations, trends, challenges, and ethical implications, as well as practical solutions related to AI-driven and cybersecurity-enabled technologies. It also seeks to foster scientific collaboration, networking, and interdisciplinary partnerships among participants from academia, industry, and research institutions.AISEC4HSG’2026 further offers PhD students and early-career researchers the opportunity to strengthen their theoretical and practical knowledge, interact with leading specialists, and explore recent scientific breakthroughs in Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Intelligent Systems, and Advanced Computing Technologies.Participants will discover emerging technologies, innovative methodologies, and real-world applications in computing, networking, intelligent systems, and cybersecurity that are driving the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence applied to healthcare and social good. Special attention will be devoted to the ethical, societal, legal, economic, and security challenges raised by the AI and cybersecurity revolution, with the aim of promoting responsible, trustworthy, and human-centered innovation.Through this event, the colloquium aims to:Provide an interdisciplinary forum to discuss innovations, challenges, and ethical implications of AI-driven and cybersecurity-enabled technologies.Foster scientific collaboration and networking among academia, industry, and research institutions.Support PhD students and early-career researchers in strengthening their theoretical and practical expertise.Explore the societal, economic, and technological impact of Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity across a wide range of application domains.Promote responsible, trustworthy, and human-centered innovation.The discussions will explore the opportunities offered by these interconnected disciplines and their societal, economic, and technological impact, particularly in the following areas:Healthcare and well-beingEducation and learningIndustryTransportationEnvironmentAgricultureEnergyClimate changeSocial and personal developmentSocial innovationSmart citiesGovernance
