postings.conferenceName: 17th Symposium on Software Performance
postings.conferenceText: The 17th Symposium on Software Performance (SSP) will take place in Würzburg, Germany, from 09 to 11 November 2026.The submission portal is now open (https://cmt3.research.microsoft.com/SSP2026).In addition to invited talks from practitioners and researchers, we welcome contributions from academic, scientific, and industrial contexts within the field of software performance. This includes, but is not limited to, approaches employing Descartes, Kieker, and/or Palladio.*Scope*Submissions are invited for plans, ongoing work, or results regarding:   *     Software quality analysis with regard to: performance; scalability and         elasticity; energy efficiency; dependability and resilience; security         and privacy   *     Application performance measurement and management   *     Performance measurement and benchmarking   *     Performance modelling (modelling concepts, simulation, extraction, and         calibration)   *     Automated run-time management of software systems   *     Automated approaches for performance problem detection, diagnosis, and         resolution   *     Performance-related challenges in industrial software systems   *     Application of Descartes, Kieker, or Palladio in projectsPlease note that we explicitly welcome contributions that have already been (partially) presented at other events or in prior publications.*Types of Contributions *We solicit the following types of contributions:   *     Technical papers (maximum 3 pages, including references)   *     Extended abstracts for industry or experience talks (max. 700 words)*Submission Guidelines *Technical papers should follow the Softwaretechnik-Trends format and must be submitted electronically via Microsoft CMT. Extended abstracts must be submitted as "abstract only" submissions (both in text and PDF format) via Microsoft CMT as well.We strongly encourage you to use our LaTeX template for your technical paper to minimize the need for adjustment if your submission is accepted. Make sure that the document uses a Times/Computer Modern font in 10 pt and that the paper size is A4.*Publication*At least one author of each accepted paper is required to register, attend the conference, and present the paper. postings.conferenceText: 3rd International Conference on Digital Sovereignty (ICDS) 2026Publisher: Springer Proceedings in Complexity (Indexed in Scopus, DBLP, WoS, Level 1 in NSD)Welcome to ICDS 2026!It is with great pleasure to welcome you to the Third International Conference on Digital Sovereignty (ICDS 2026), which will be organised by the Institute for Energy Technology (IFE) from November 25th – 27th, 2026, in Oslo, Norway.The International Conference on Digital Sovereignty (ICDS) is the world’s only dedicated conference exclusively focused on digital sovereignty, addressing one of the most critical challenges shaping today’s digital future. Established in 2024, ICDS has rapidly emerged as a unique global platform where policy, industry, and cutting-edge research converge to build trust, resilience, and autonomy in advanced digital ecosystems. The conference is distinctly structured into three complementary pillars: a high-level Industry Day, where global technology leaders openly discuss real-world strategies and challenges in implementing digital sovereignty; practical training sessions that translate policy and innovation into actionable capabilities; and peer-reviewed research presentations, where leading researchers from top institutions present solutions across technological, legal, and societal dimensions of digital sovereignty. Building on the strong foundations of ICDS 2024 and the expanded international impact of ICDS 2025, the 3rd International Conference on Digital Sovereignty (ICDS 2026) will further strengthen Norway’s leadership at the forefront of global digital policy, innovation, and research, welcoming the international community to Oslo to shape the future of sovereign, secure, and sustainable digital infrastructure.  As in ICDS 2025, selected papers from the ICDS 2026 conference will be published in the Springer Proceedings on Complexity, further reinforcing the conference’s scientific quality and international visibility.Call for PapersWe have five tracks in ICDS 2026. Papers in any of these areas, especially with the following keywords covering and related to Digital Sovereignty, are welcome to be submitted.Track 1: Human-Centric Digital SovereigntyTrack 2: Industry and Innovation ImpactTrack 3: Digital Ecosystems and GovernanceTrack 4: National Digital Sovereignty and Societal ImpactTrack 5: Geopolitics and TrustPrevious EditionsICDS 2024 – publication: Elsevier Procedia Computer Science https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/procedia-computer-science/vol/254/suppl/CICDS 2025 – publication: Springer Proceedings in Complexity (SPCOM) https://link.springer.com/book/9783032215239Submission: https://easychair.org/my/conference?conf=icds20260The ICDS 2025 c onference is now in the process of soliciting submissions of original and innovative papers. Prospective authors are invited to submit papers in core and/or related areas of digital sovereignty. The detailed list of topics can be found in the ‘Call for Papers’. Each paper will be reviewed by three experts from the International Program Committee.Authors must submit an original full paper, 10 pages for Springer Proceedings on Complexity, that has not been previously published. All contributions must be written in English. Submissions will be evaluated based on relevance to conference themes (digital sovereignty, cybersecurity, data governance), originality and novelty, technical quality and rigor, clarity and organization, impact and significance, and, where applicable, ethical and responsible research practices, especially in areas such as AI and data use.Submission GuidelinesSubmissions to ICDS 2026 will follow a rigorous and transparent review process to ensure high-quality contributions. After the submission deadline, all papers will be screened by the editors for relevance and baseline quality. Suitable submissions will then be peer-reviewed by at least three independent experts. The editors will carefully evaluate the reviews and make recommendations based on consensus and merit. Finally, accepted papers will be reviewed by the chairs’ Steering Committee and Honorary Chair for final confirmation. Our goal is to maintain fairness, academic integrity, and constructive feedback throughout the process.Authors must submit an original full paper (6 -10 pages) that has not previously been published. All contributions must be written in English.Instructions for Authors of Springer Computer Science postings.conferenceName: Call for Book Reviews - Journal for Cultural and Religious Theory
postings.conferenceText: The editorial board of the Journal for Cultural and Religious Theory (JCRT), a Whitestone Publication, is pleased to announce the relaunch of its book review program. Effective immediately, JCRT is soliciting single-title reviews and cluster reviews from scholars working across religious studies, theology, philosophy of religion, critical theory, and adjacent fields.The relaunch responds directly to the void left by the closure of Reading Religion, the American Academy of Religion’s openly accessible book review site, which ceased active operations on May 31, 2026. With one of the largest open venues for scholarly religion reviews now transitioned to an archive, JCRT aims to help fill that gap by offering an open-access, peer-edited home for rigorous, timely, and theoretically engaged reviews.A call to a broad community of reviewersJCRT especially encourages graduate students and independent scholars to submit reviews, alongside tenure-track and established faculty. The editorial board views the relaunched review section as both a venue for serious critical engagement and an opportunity for emerging scholars to build publication records, sharpen their voices, and contribute to ongoing conversations in cultural and religious theory.“We want the review section to reflect the full range of scholars doing important work in our fields — from first-year doctoral students to senior colleagues,” said J.C. Smith, the book review editor. “Independent scholars and graduate students often produce the most incisive and generative reviews, and JCRT is committed to being a home for that work.”Submission formatsJCRT invites two primary formats:Individual book reviews — approximately 1,500 words, engaging a single recent title.Cluster reviews — approximately 2,000–2,500 words, engaging two to three thematically related titles in conversation.Reviews should combine substantive summary with critical, theoretically informed engagement consistent with JCRT’s longstanding editorial vision.How to submit or propose a reviewScholars interested in reviewing for JCRT — whether proposing a specific title, responding to a call, or offering to be added to the reviewer pool — should email the Book Review Editor at editor@jcrt.org with the subject line “JCRT-Review.” Please include a brief statement of interest, areas of expertise, and (if applicable) the title or titles you propose to review.Full submission guidelines are available at https://jcrt.org/submissions/About JCRTThe Journal for Cultural and Religious Theory is an open-access, peer-reviewed journal published by Whitestone Publications. Since its founding, JCRT has served as a leading venue for interdisciplinary work at the intersections of religion, theology, philosophy, and cultural theory, publishing scholars from around the world.ContactContact: JC Smith, Book Review Editor, editor@jcrt.orgWeb: https://jcrt.org###

postings.conferenceName: 1st Workshop on Decentralisation: Theory and Practice
postings.conferenceText: We invite submissions to the 1st Workshop on Decentralisation: Theory and Practice (DeTaP), to be held in association with Advances in Financial Technologies (AFT) 2026.Topics of interest include, but are not limited to:- Definitions and conceptualisations of decentralisation- Methods for measuring decentralisation- Critiques and limitations of existing measurement frameworks- Empirical studies of decentralisation in deployed systems- Decentralisation of blockchain governance- Legal tests for decentralisation and their relationship to technical definitions- Liability and accountability in decentralised systems- Optimal or “sufficient” degrees of decentralisation- Trade-offs between decentralisation and other system properties (e.g. efficiency, scalability, accountability)- Decentralisation of blockchain hardware and infrastructure- Case studies of endogenous and exogenous events shaping decentralisation- Causal analysis: drivers of decentralisation and centralisation pressures- Normative arguments for or against decentralisation- Decentralisation in other fields vs. blockchain-specific framing- Historical and non-blockchain case studies of decentralised systems, successful or unsuccessfulSubmissions require only a title and abstract describing the proposed talk. Authors may optionally submit a full or short paper alongside the abstract.The workshop has no proceedings and is intended as a venue for exchanging ideas, therefore work in progress and work that has been published at or submitted to another venue is equally welcome.Accepted papers may optionally be made available on the workshop's website at the authors' discretion.Submissions should be made via this form: https://forms.gle/3XGwZN2MbaG3vAZm6

postings.conferenceName: Special Session on Computational Methods for Intelligent Biofabrication: Models, Data and Reproducible Benchmarks - CompBioFab - Within BIOSTEC 2027
postings.conferenceText: Biofabrication, the automated generation of functional constructs from cells, biomaterials and bioactive molecules, still relies on trial-and-error design, and the cost of wet-lab iterations makes exhaustive experimentation infeasible. Intelligent Biofabrication replaces this with model-based, predictive engineering: simulators of cellular behaviour, hybrid multi-scale models and digital twins, protocol optimisation, and data-driven approaches learning from accumulated evidence.The CompBioFab Special Session, held within BIOSTEC 2027 in Valletta, Malta, is organised around interdisciplinary convergence, structured around shared benchmark problems, datasets and evaluation protocols. We invite submission of full papers and abstracts on the following topics of interest:- Multiscale Cellular Modeling: molecular to construct-scale formalisms, coupled- Biohybrid Robotics: living tissue fused with synthetic actuation- Computational & AI Biofabrication: machine learning for protocol design- Datasets & Reproducible Benchmarks: shared standards & evaluation protocols- Digital Twins & Bioreactors: simulated bioreactor processes & controls- Calibration & Uncertainty Quantification: validating models against experimental data- Organoids & In Vitro Models: New Approach Methodologies (NAMs)- Sustainable, Automated Workflows: resource-aware, reusable computational pipelinesPlease refer to the BIOSTEC 2027 submission guidelines for full paper/abstract formatting instructions.SUBMISSION LINK: https://biostec.scitevents.org/CompBioFabCO-CHAIRS Roberta Bardini, Politecnico di Torino, Italy Laurence Calzone, Institut Curie, France Miriam Filippi, ETH Zurich, Switzerland Diana Massai, Politecnico di Torino, ItalyCONTACT biostec.secretariat@insticc.org roberta.bardini@polito.it

postings.conferenceName: The 2nd International Workshop on Deep Learning for Biometrics and its Applications
postings.conferenceText: The 2nd International Workshop on Deep Learning for Biometrics and its Applications (DL4BA) will be held at Phoenix, Arizona, USA, in hybrid mode, from 14 to 17 december 2025, in conjunction with the IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData 2026, https://bigdataieee.org/BigData2026/).OverviewBiometrics has become a burgeoning research area due to the industrial and government needs for authentication, identification, security, and privacy concerns. Biometric technology has become useful solution for various applications including access control, surveillance and privacy, hardware security and forensics. During last decade, Deep Learning (DL) has received a great attention to solve difficult and complex problems in various domains. Its ability to automatically learn features from big data has made it a major asset.This workshop aims to present and discuss the recent advances on deep learning applied to biometrics providing innovative solutions to challenging problems in biometrics. It is an opportunity to bring researchers and experts together to discuss the current and future state of biometrics.Topics of interest include, but are not limited to, the following:- DL for biometrics-based authentication and identification- Deep biometric feature extraction- Deep biometric feature fusion- DL for biometric data analytics (signal, image, video, ...)- DL for biometric spoofing and deepfake detection- DL for big data challenges in biometrics- DL for multimodal biometrics- DL for soft biometrics- DL for forensic biometrics- DL for biometric security and privacy- Leveraging DL techniques for biometrics- Generative AI in biometrics- Federated learning in biometrics - Related applicationsImportant DatesOct. 1, 2026 (11:59 pm CST): Due date for full workshop papers submissionNov. 4, 2026: Notification of paper acceptance to authorsNov. 25, 2026: Camera-ready of accepted papersDec 14-17, 2026: WorkshopsPaper submissionPlease submit a full-length paper (up to 10 pages IEEE 2-column format including references) or a short-length paper (5 to 7 pages including references) through the online submission system (https://wi-lab.com/cyberchair/2026/bigdata26/index.php)Papers should be formatted to IEEE Computer Society Proceedings Manuscript Formatting Guidelines. See link to "formatting instructions" here : https://www.ieee.org/conferences/publishing/templates.htmlElectronic submissions in PDF format are required.All papers accepted for this workshop will be published in the Workshop Proceedings of IEEE Big Data Conference, made available in the IEEE eXplore digital library.Online Submission :https://wi-lab.com/cyberchair/2026/bigdata26/scripts/submit.php?subarea=S02&undisplay_detail=1&wh=/cyberchair/2026/bigdata26/scripts/ws_submit.phpPublicationAll accepted papers will be published in the IEEE Big Data proceedings and IEEE Xplore Digital Library.ContactProf. Larbi Boubchir (Workshop Chair)University of Paris 8, FranceE-mail: larbi.boubchir@univ-paris8.fr

postings.conferenceText: CALL FOR PAPERS5th International Workshop on Blockchain Security and Scalability (BSS 2026)Co-located with IEEE Blockchain 202630 November–4 December 2026Université Marie et Louis Pasteur, Montbéliard, FranceWorkshop date: 30 November–4 December 2026 web: www.ibss.comABOUT THE WORKSHOPThe 5th International Workshop on Blockchain Security and Scalability (BSS 2026) invites researchers and practitioners from academia, industry and government to submit original research on the foundations, design, implementation and evaluation of blockchain and distributed ledger technologies.Blockchain systems support decentralised coordination across finance, healthcare, logistics, e-government, the Internet of Things, cyber-physical systems and next-generation networks. However, security weaknesses, privacy risks and scalability constraints continue to limit dependable real-world adoption.BSS 2026 provides a focused forum for research that addresses these challenges. The workshop welcomes theoretical work, system designs, empirical studies, reproducible evaluations, datasets, testbeds, case studies and critical analyses of deployed systems. postings.conferenceName: Knowledge and Natural Language Processing Track @ ACM SAC 2027
postings.conferenceText: Knowledge and Natural Language Processing Track @ ACM SAC 2027Aim and ScopeThe Knowledge and Natural Language Processing (KNLP) Track at the ACM Symposium on Applied Computing investigates methods and applications at the intersection of Knowledge Engineering and Natural Language Processing, with particular emphasis on approaches that combine these two areas.KNLP is an emerging and highly interdisciplinary research field at the core of Artificial Intelligence. It brings together and complements scientific advances in Natural Language Processing, Knowledge Representation and Reasoning, Machine Learning, and related disciplines.Topics of InterestTopics of interest include, but are not limited to, the following.Natural Language Processing    NLP methods for knowledge extraction    NLP for ontology population and ontology learning    Sentiment analysis and opinion mining for knowledge-based applications    Interplay between natural language and ontologies    NLP for explainable knowledge    Machine translation techniques for multilingual knowledge    NLP for the Web    Bias detection and mitigation in small and large language models    Interaction between small or large language models and knowledgeKnowledge    Knowledge-enhanced NLP    Knowledge for information retrieval    Knowledge-based sentiment analysis and opinion mining    Combining knowledge and deep learning for NLP    Knowledge technologies for the Web    Knowledge-enhanced agentic reasoning    Agent reasoning over knowledge graphs and ontologies    Knowledge-based agent personalization    Linked Data for NLP    Knowledge-based natural language explainability    Language-model-enhanced ontology and knowledge engineering methodologies and tools    Language-model-based agents for knowledge extraction, reasoning, and management    Ontology evaluation using small and large language models    Ontological knowledge representation and memorization in language models    Knowledge-based techniques for language models, including Retrieval-Augmented Generation, fact-checking, and bias mitigation    Question answering over knowledge graphs using small and large language modelsReal-World Applications Exploiting Knowledge and NLP    Knowledge and NLP systems for Big Data scenarios    Knowledge and NLP technologies supporting a diverse, equitable, and inclusive society    Deployment and evaluation of Knowledge and NLP systems in domains such as:        Digital Humanities and Social Sciences        eGovernment and public administration        Life sciences, healthcare, and medicine        News, media, and data-streaming environmentsPaper SubmissionWe invite original research papers and experience reports addressing the topics listed above.Submissions must not have been previously published or be under consideration for publication elsewhere. Papers must be submitted in PDF format using the official ACM SAC proceedings template.Authors’ names and affiliations must be entered separately in the submission system and must not appear in the submitted manuscript. All submissions will undergo a double-blind peer-review process in accordance with ACM SAC regulations.Submissions to the Student Research Competition (SRC) are also welcome. Prospective authors should consult the SAC 2027 SRC page for eligibility requirements and submission instructions.Submission Policy    All papers must initially be submitted as regular papers. There is no separate submission category for poster papers.    Papers will be evaluated according to their originality, technical contribution, presentation quality, and relevance to the Knowledge and Natural Language Processing Track.    Depending on the outcome of the review process and the overall acceptance-rate constraints, technically sound submissions that cannot be accepted as regular papers may be offered acceptance as posters.    Although there is no formal minimum page requirement, submissions shorter than four full pages that do not demonstrate a substantial contribution may be desk-rejected without external review.Submission Links    Regular papers and SRC abstracts: submission links are available through the ACM SAC 2027 website    Author kit and templates: formatting instructions and official templates are available through the ACM SAC 2027 websiteImportant DatesPlease consult the official ACM SAC 2027 website for up-to-date deadlines and possible changes.    October 2, 2026: Regular paper and SRC abstract submission    November 13, 2026: Author notification    November 28, 2026: Camera-ready copies of accepted papers and SRC submissions    December 5, 2026: Author registration deadline    April 5–9, 2027: Knowledge and Natural Language Processing Track at ACM SAC 2027All deadlines follow the time zone specified on the official conference website.Further InformationFor further information, please visit the Knowledge and Natural Language Processing Track website and the ACM SAC 2027 conference website.Questions may be addressed to the KNLP Track Co-Chairs.

postings.conferenceName: 1st Workshop on Virtual ISA for Rapidly Evolving Architectures @ MICRO 2026
postings.conferenceText: VISA 2026 examines the virtual ISA — a stable, hardware-agnostic abstraction between high-level programming models and diverse hardware backends — as the pivotal interface of the agentic era: the contract surface where LLM-driven code synthesizers, autonomous autotuners, compilers, and microarchitectural innovation meet. When the programmer is a machine, the ISA must be self-describing enough to reason over and verifiable enough to trust.The accelerator landscape is undergoing rapid and continuous transformation. However, this rapid architectural evolution introduces a critical fragmentation problem: each accelerator spawns its own toolchain, compiler backend, and software stack, leading to duplicated engineering effort, poor portability, and steep developer learning curves across targets. Virtual ISA enables compiler reuse across heterogeneous targets, rapid hardware prototyping, software longevity across architectural generations, and composable optimization at the right abstraction level.Despite this progress, the community lacks a dedicated venue for the cross-cutting challenges of Virtual ISA design, compilation, DSL integration, and co-design — the gap this workshop aims to fill.We invite short papers (4–6 pages, IEEE format) describing work in progress, position papers, vision papers, or early results. The scope spans the full accelerator stack — ISA design and semantics, compilation and optimization, DSLs and programming models, hardware co-design, and deployment experience.The agent-facing interface is the flagship theme that runs through all of them: wherever your work sits, we encourage you to ask how the problem changes when the primary reader and writer of the ISA is a machine.TOPICS OF INTERESTTopics include, but are not limited to:1. Agent-Facing Virtual ISA Interfaces- Self-describing virtual ISAs exposing semantics, costs, and resource footprints to LLM reasoners- Well-typed and verifiable contracts for reliable agent-generated code- Equivalence checking for machine-generated kernels- LLM-guided lowering and kernel synthesis- Closed-loop autotuning through the virtual ISA layer- Safety and sandboxing for agent-generated kernels- Benchmarks for the agent-programmability of virtual ISAs- Self-evolving virtual ISAs and lowering strategies2. Virtual ISA Design and Abstraction- Stable virtual ISA boundaries- Formal semantics and correctness- Versioning and compatibility strategies- Capability negotiation, feature discovery, and introspection- Effect systems, memory models, and concurrency semantics- Abstractions for heterogeneous architectures3. Virtual ISA and Architecture Co-design- Late binding of physical resources during virtual-to-physical lowering- Cost-model-aware virtual ISAs- Interfaces for parallelism, dataflow, precision, and locality- Reconfigurable and spatial architectures- Emerging hardware features and accelerator architectures- Dynamic-shape execution under stable semantics- Programmability–performance tradeoffs- AI acceleration, LLM serving, MoE, sparsity, processing-in-memory, chiplets, and KV-cache-oriented systems4. Compiler Optimizations- Lowering and legalization targeting virtual ISAs- Optimization across virtual and physical ISA boundaries- Polyhedral, tile-level, and search-based optimization- Profile-guided compilation- Equivalence checking and differential testing- LLM-aware compilation- Kernel fusion, scheduling, and graph partitioning- Directive- and annotation-guided compilation5. DSLs and Programming Models- Tile, dataflow, graph, and agentic pipeline languages- DSL frontends targeting virtual ISAs- Type systems for accelerator programming- Autotuning and search-based code generation- Programming abstractions for emerging AI workloads- LLM inference and training, MoE routing, long-context attention, KV-cache management, and multimodal or agentic serving- Profiling APIs and feedback-driven optimization6. Case Studies and Infrastructure- Virtual ISA deployments in AI, HPC, networking, and signal processing- Open-source frameworks and benchmarks- Simulation, modeling, and hardware/software co-design flows- Production experience with MLIR dialects, PTX, SPIR-V, StableHLO, TOSA, Triton-IR, CUDA Tile IR, Ascend PTO, and related systemsSUBMISSION GUIDELINESPaper length:4–6 pages using the IEEE conference two-column template.Paper types:Work-in-progress papers, position papers, vision papers, and early-results papers are welcome.Reviewing:The review process is single-blind. Author names and affiliations should appear in the submission.Submission site:https://visa2026.hotcrp.com/The HotCRP site is currently pending activation. Submissions will open after approval.Publication:Accepted papers will be presented at the workshop and posted on the VISA 2026 website. The workshop is non-archival, and submission does not preclude later publication at another venue.Presentation:At least one author of every accepted paper must register for the workshop through MICRO 2026 and present the work.Review process:Every submission will receive at least three reviews. Papers will be evaluated for relevance, originality, soundness, and potential to spark discussion.IMPORTANT DATESPaper submission deadline:September 25, 2026, 23:59 AoEAuthor notification:October 9, 2026, 23:59 AoECamera-ready papers:October 16, 2026, 23:59 AoEWorkshop:October 31, 202613:00–17:00 EETAthens, GreeceCONTACT AND FURTHER INFORMATIONWorkshop website:https://visaworkshop.github.io/2026/Call for Papers:https://visaworkshop.github.io/2026/cfp.htmlContact:visa.workshop.chairs@gmail.com

postings.conferenceText: Conference Theme+The DHARTI 2026 Biennial Conference seeks to foreground Digital Humanities as a critical site for interrogating questions of social justice, digital inclusion, digital justice, infrastructural access, representation, and epistemic inequality in and with the majority world.As digital and algorithmic technologies increasingly shape contemporary modes of knowledge production, pedagogy, archives, media circulation, and cultural participation, it becomes necessary to critically examine the uneven structures through which digitality operates. The conference aims to explore how Digital Humanities can move beyond techno-deterministic frameworks toward more inclusive, multilingual, community-oriented, and socially grounded practices.The conference welcomes scholars, researchers, educators, artists, archivists, technologists, activists, community practitioners, students, and engaged stakeholders across and beyond disciplines.Select papers will be published in a Scopus-Indexed Volume. The conference invites contributions on, but not limited to, the following areas, with a particular focus on Global Majority spaces and contexts:Decolonial tools and Decolonising Practices in Digital HumanitiesDigital Justice, Infrastructural Inequalities and Digital FuturesDigital Justice and Literary and Cultural ExpressionsCollaborative Knowledge Production and Digital SpaceArchives, Memory, and Digital PreservationLanguage Technologies and Multilingual FuturesDigital Pedagogy and Curricular representation and perspectives.In-person Poster Presentations: For emerging projects and research initiatives.Proposals for Workshops: The conference will be preceded by a set of pre-conference workshops. DHARTI members can propose workshops. Workshops will be scheduled on 18 Dec 2026 (Fri.).No participant shall serve as a lead presenter in more than one presentation. In the event that a presenter is shortlisted as a lead presenter for two or more papers after the review process, the Programme Committee will ask the participant to withdraw one of the papers. However, where an abstract or poster is submitted in an Indian language, an English version must also be provided to ensure that the content is accessible to the larger conference audience.All participants are required to be members of DHARTI (Digital Humanities Alliance for Research and Teaching Innovation). Those who wish to continue their membership beyond that period may register according to the prescribed membership criteria.Selected papers, following peer review and editorial evaluation, will be considered for publication in an edited conference proceedings volume.KIIT has secured a Letter of Intent from Peter Lang, an internationally reputed academic publisher, indicating its willingness to consider a select number of conference papers for publication. postings.conferenceName: 18th International Conference on Deontic Logic and Normative Systems, 29 June–1 July 2027, Hangzhou, China (First announcement)
postings.conferenceText: Dear colleagues,We are pleased to announce that DEON 2027, the 18th International Conference on Deontic Logic and Normative Systems, will be held at Zhejiang University in Hangzhou, China, from 29 June to 1 July 2027 — the first edition of the series to be held in Asia since its founding in 1991. The conference is hosted by the School of Philosophy of Zhejiang University and the Zhejiang University–University of Luxembourg Joint Lab on Advanced Intelligent Systems and Reasoning (ZLAIRE).The biennial DEON conference series brings together researchers interested in the formal study of normative concepts, normative reasoning, and normative systems, using methods from computer science, artificial intelligence, philosophy, linguistics, mathematics, and law. Topics include deontic logic, normative reasoning, legal reasoning, normative multi-agent systems, explainability, and trustworthy systems (full list on the website).The general theme of this edition is "Normativity under Uncertainty". Normative systems are inescapably confronted with uncertainty: agents must frequently deliberate about what ought to be done on the basis of information that is incomplete, imprecise, or conflicting — about the facts of the case, the norms in force, the consequences of action, or the reliability of one's sources. This edition investigates how central normative concepts, among them obligation, permission, responsibility, and blame, can be rigorously formalized, interpreted, and applied once the classical idealizations of certainty, consistency, and full information are lifted.Key dates (all Anywhere on Earth):Abstract submission deadline: 5 March 2027Paper submission deadline: 12 March 2027Notification of acceptance: 6 May 2027Conference: 29 June – 1 July 2027The conference will invite submissions of original and unpublished work (max. 15 pages, excluding references and technical appendix); reviewing will be double-blind. The proceedings will be published by College Publications as an open-access book. The full call for papers, including templates and the EasyChair submission link, will be released in November 2026.Programme committee co-chairs:Huimin Dong (TU Wien, Austria)Beishui Liao (Zhejiang University, China)Réka Markovich (University of Luxembourg, Luxembourg)Website: https://www.zlaire.net/deon2027/Contact: zhengzhoulogic@zju.edu.cnPlease save the date, and feel free to forward this announcement to interested colleagues and students.Best regards,The DEON 2027 Programme Committee Co-Chairs

postings.conferenceText: ======================================================================CALL FOR PAPERS -- AID 20262nd IEEE PRDC Workshop on AI Dependability======================================================================Held in conjunction with the 31st IEEE Pacific Rim International Symposium on Dependable Computing (PRDC 2026).Where: Hong Kong SARWhen: one day within 2-4 December 2026 (the exact day will be announced on the workshop website)Website: https://aid2026-workshop.github.ioSubmit: https://easychair.org/conferences/?conf=aid2026))) PAPER SUBMISSION DEADLINE: 11 SEPTEMBER 2026 (AoE) (((======================================================================----------------------------------------------------------------------SCOPE----------------------------------------------------------------------The AID 2026 workshop provides a forum for researchers and industry practitioners to present and discuss the latest advancements in ensuring the dependability of AI and LLM-based systems. As AI becomes integral to critical infrastructure, its reliability, security, and robustness are paramount. This workshop will bring together experts from the dependable computing and AI communities to address new challenges in building trustable AI systems. We welcome submissions that explore innovative solutions, case studies, and fundamental research in this rapidly evolving field.----------------------------------------------------------------------TOPICS OF INTEREST----------------------------------------------------------------------Topics include but are not limited to:* AI-based Software Vulnerability Detection and Secure Code Generation* AI-based Attack Detection* LLM-based Rust Translation* AI-based Attack/Defense Simulation* AI-based Red Teaming* AI Model Attacks and Defenses* AI Dependability, Reliability, and Safety* Responsible and Trustworthy AI* Explainable AI (XAI)----------------------------------------------------------------------TWO SUBMISSION TRACKS----------------------------------------------------------------------* Regular Paper Track. Completed research, presented as a full conference paper with a clear contribution and supporting evaluation.* R&D Paper Track. Research carried out under a funded research project and still in progress. Papers introduce the project's objectives and approach and report interim findings, giving project teams a venue to present ongoing work and gather feedback.----------------------------------------------------------------------SUBMISSION GUIDELINES----------------------------------------------------------------------* Length. Original, unpublished, and not under review elsewhere.* Submission. Through EasyChair: https://easychair.org/conferences/?conf=aid2026----------------------------------------------------------------------PUBLICATION----------------------------------------------------------------------Accepted papers from both tracks will be published by the IEEE Computer Society Press (EI indexed) as part of the PRDC 2026 proceedings.----------------------------------------------------------------------IMPORTANT DATES (AoE)----------------------------------------------------------------------* Paper submission: 11 September 2026* Author notification: 9 October 2026* Camera ready submission: 20 October 2026----------------------------------------------------------------------COMMITTEES----------------------------------------------------------------------ORGANIZATION CHAIRS* Huy Kang Kim, Korea University* Dan Dongseong Kim, University of Queensland* Sangkyun Lee, Korea UniversityPROGRAM CHAIR* Hyunjae Kang, University of QueenslandPROGRAM COMMITTEE* Ah Reum Kang, Pai Chai University* Byung Il Kwak, Korea University* Hyoungshick Kim, Sungkyunkwan University* Hyun Min Song, Dankook University* Jeonghyun Lee, National Security Research Institute* Jiyoung Woo, Soonchunhyang University* Ke He, University of Canterbury* Ki-Woong Park, Sejong University* Mee Lan Han, Korea University* Mengmeng Ge, Monash University* Sang-Hoon Choi, Sejong University* Sanghoon Jeon, Kookmin University* Seonghoon Jeong, Sookmyung Women's University* Seungjin Ryu, National Security Research Institute* Taekyoung Kwon, Yonsei University======================================================================

postings.conferenceName: Service-Oriented Computing for AI Applications
postings.conferenceText: The 3rd Workshop on Service-Oriented Computing for AI Applications (SOC4AI 2026) is an accepted workshop of the 24th International Conference on Service-Oriented Computing (ICSOC 2026). It will be held in person in Lodz, Poland, on 1 December 2026.Service-Oriented Computing (SOC) has transformed the engineering of distributed software systems over the past two decades, while Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping every facet of the digital economy. SOC4AI 2026 brings these two domains into a single forum to explore synergies, challenges, and emerging research directions.The workshop pursues a dual objective:1) Service-Oriented Computing for AI ApplicationsHow SOC principles, standards, and middleware can accelerate the design, deployment, and life-cycle management of AI-centric systems spanning the cloud-edge continuum.Topics include, but are not limited to:    Service-based AI architectures and reference architectures for machine-learning and generative AI pipelines.    AI as a Service, including lightweight service descriptions and ontologies for foundation-model APIs.    Orchestration and composition of AI services across heterogeneous providers and execution environments.    Scalable, elastic, and cost-aware deployment of AI services across cloud, edge, and continuum infrastructures.    Governance, privacy, security, compliance, and observability in service-based AI deployments.2) AI for Service-Oriented ComputingHow contemporary AI techniques, including foundation models, reinforcement learning, and causal inference, can enrich, automate, and optimise service-oriented architectures from discovery and composition to monitoring, governance, and sustainability.Topics include, but are not limited to:    Intelligent service discovery, matching, recommendation, and composition.    Autonomous service management, self-optimisation, policy enforcement, and runtime adaptation.    LLM copilots and agents for service operation, engineering, monitoring, and governance.    Predictive analytics, anomaly detection, and maintenance for service-oriented systems.    Sustainable and cost-efficient service operations using AI-driven placement, scaling, and resource management.Key Themes:SOC4AI 2026 particularly welcomes contributions on interoperable AI service ecosystems, AI-powered autonomy and governance, sustainable and cost-efficient service operations, and human-centric and responsible AI-as-a-Service.By convening researchers and practitioners from both communities, SOC4AI 2026 will consolidate best practices, surface emerging pain points, and articulate a shared roadmap for the next generation of intelligent, service-driven computing, aligned with the core topics of ICSOC.Target Audience:    Researchers in SOC, cloud/edge computing, and AI/ML.    Industrial R&D engineers building AI platforms, marketplaces, and service ecosystems.    PhD students seeking cross-disciplinary perspectives.    Standards bodies and open-source community representatives.Submission:Workshop papers should be 8–12 pages long and use the Springer LNCS format. Paper submissions are due on 23 September 2026 at 23:59 AOE. Each paper will receive at least three reviews.Submit through the ICSOC 2026 EasyChair submission system and select the SOC4AI 2026 workshop track when creating your submission. See the complete submission instructions and important dates.

postings.conferenceName: 34th International Colloquium On Structural Information and Communication Complexity
postings.conferenceText: =====================================SIROCCO 2027 Call for Papers=====================================34th International Colloquium On Structural Information and Communication ComplexityLarnaca, Cyprus, June 2–4, 2027, https://cyprusconferences.org/sirocco2027=====================================Important Dates=====================================Full paper submission: October 31, 2026 (AoE)Paper notification: January 30, 2027Conference dates: June 2–4, 2027=====================================About SIROCCO=====================================SIROCCO is devoted to the study of the interplay between structural knowledge, communication, and computing in decentralized systems that consist of multiple communicating entities. Special emphasis is given to innovative methodological and solution approaches that lead to a better understanding of the relationship between computing and communication.SIROCCO has a tradition of interesting and productive scientific meetings in a relaxed and pleasant atmosphere, attracting leading researchers in a variety of fields in which communication and knowledge play a significant role. Websites of past SIROCCO conferences can be found at https://sirocco.hiit.fi. The proceedings of past SIROCCO conferences can be found at https://link.springer.com/conference/sirocco.=====================================Scope=====================================Original papers are solicited from all areas of study of local structural knowledge and global communication and computational complexities.Typical but not exclusive topics of interest include the following (in alphabetical order).•	Biological and nature-inspired distributed algorithms•	Blockchains and related distributed paradigms•	Distributed algorithms and computability•	Distributed graph algorithms•	Distributed quantum computing•	Epistemic modeling and analysis of distributed systems•	Fault tolerance•	Formal verification of distributed systems•	Game theory in distributed computing•	Mobile agents and autonomous distributed systems•	Network modeling and analysis•	Security in distributed computing•	Self-stabilization•	Shared-memory algorithms•	Structural and communication complexity analysis•	Topology in distributed computing•	Wireless, ad-hoc, and peer-to-peer networksKeeping with the tradition of SIROCCO, submissions on new areas related to the general scope of the conference are also welcome.=====================================Submission Instructions=====================================Submissions must report on original research and contain results that have not appeared previously in a regular conference paper and that have not been concurrently submitted to or previously published in a journal or a conference with published proceedings.Submission format. Manuscripts must be submitted in PDF format using EasyChair. Submissions must be written in English and formatted in a single-column format on US letter-size or A4 paper, use at least 11-point font, and have at least 2.5 cm margins.Submission length. All submissions must start with a cover page, which will include the paper’s title, a short abstract, and, preferably, keywords.There is no page limit, and authors are encouraged to submit the full version of their paper. The submission should contain, within the first 12 pages (excluding the cover page and bibliographic references), a concise and clear presentation of the primary content and merits of the work.Content beyond the cover page, references, and the first 12 pages will be read at the discretion of the reviewers only.A submission that is not accepted as a full paper may be invited as a brief announcement.Double-blind reviewing. SIROCCO 2027 will employ a lightweight double-blind reviewing process. Submissions should not reveal the identity of the authors in any way (e.g., author names, affiliations, email addresses, and funding information should not appear in the submission). However, authors are free to disseminate draft versions of their submissions as they normally would (e.g., by posting drafts on the web). Questions about the double-blind reviewing process may be directed to the PC chair by email.Submission website. Paper submissions will be handled by EasyChair, so please make sure that you have an active account. Papers must be submitted electronically at https://easychair.org/conferences/?conf=sirocco2027.Submissions deviating from these guidelines as well as papers outside the general scope of the conference may be rejected without consideration of their merits.=====================================AI policy=====================================AI policy for authors.  All authors of a submission must be human and are fully responsible for the integrity, originality, and copyright of their submission.Authors may use AI tools for limited purposes such as language editing (e.g., fixing typos or improving grammar) without the need for disclosure.Any other use of AI tools (including LLMs) must be clearly disclosed in the submission in an AI-disclosure section, and authors must specify which tool was used and for what purpose.Any undisclosed use of AI tools, or inaccurate representation of AI-generated or AI-modified content, may lead to rejection of the submission or further action.AI policy for reviewers.  Reviewers may use LLM-based tools to assist with the review process, provided that the confidentiality of the content of the submissions is preserved. However, the review itself must be written solely by the reviewer and must not be drafted, generated, or rewritten with the assistance of AI tools.Reviewers must rely on their own judgment and retain full responsibility for the content and conclusions of their reviews.=====================================Proceedings=====================================The proceedings of SIROCCO 2027 will be published by Springer in the Lecture Notes in Computer Science (LNCS) series. Please note that inclusion in the proceedings requires an in-person presentation by one of the authors at the conference and at least one full registration for each paper.=====================================Best Paper Awards=====================================All regular papers are eligible for the best paper award. Moreover, all regular papers with at least one student author, where the student author(s) have contributed most of the work, are also eligible for the best student paper award. If a submission is eligible for the best student paper award, please state this on the cover page.The Program Committee may choose not to make the awards or to split them among multiple papers.=====================================Special Issue=====================================Selected papers from SIROCCO 2027 will be invited to a special issue of the journal Theoretical Computer Science.=====================================Program Committee=====================================Emmanuelle Anceaume - CNRS, IRISA, Université de RennesJames Aspnes - Yale UniversityHagit Attiya - TechnionAlkida Balliu - Gran Sasso Science Institute (Chair)Petra Berenbrink - University of HamburgQuentin Bramas - University of StrasbourgYi-Jun Chang - National University of SingaporeArtur Czumaj - University of WarwickFrancesco d'Amore - Gran Sasso Science InstitutePeter Davies-Peck - Durham UniversityMichael Elkin - Ben-Gurion University of the NegevLaurent Feuilloley - CNRS, LIRIS, Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1Orr Fischer - University of HaifaMaxime Flin - Aalto UniversityPierre Fraigniaud - CNRS, IRIF, Université Paris CitéDiana Ghinea - Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and ArtsGeorge Giakkoupis - Inria, Université de RennesMagnús M. postings.conferenceName: 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Cyber Physical Systems
postings.conferenceText: The International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Cyber Physical Systems (CICPS 2027) aims to provide a dynamic and interdisciplinary platform to explore the convergence of Computational Intelligence (CI) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS)—a fusion that is transforming the way we design, operate, and secure the intelligent systems of tomorrow.Computational Intelligence techniques—rooted in nature-inspired, adaptive, and learning-based algorithms—offer innovative solutions for complex, uncertain, and nonlinear real-world problems. On the other hand, Cyber-Physical Systems represent a new generation of engineered systems that tightly integrate computation, networking, and physical processes, often interacting with human supervisors.Together, these disciplines are driving technological breakthroughs across sectors such as autonomous systems, agriculture, aerospace, infrastructure, energy, environmental monitoring, healthcare, manufacturing, and transportation. CICPS 2027 will convene top researchers, practitioners, and industry leaders to showcase state-of-the-art innovations and chart a course for future developments that promise profound societal and economic impact.

postings.conferenceName: Stories of Collective Authorship in Architecture
postings.conferenceText: Call for papersStories of Collective Authorship in ArchitectureA building is never the work of a single mind. Architectural production unfolds through the coordinated activity of many actors—designers, technicians, and administrators as well as things, technologies, and environments. The list goes on. Yet architectural culture has long narrated the built environment through the figure of the singular author: the master architect whose name becomes synonymous with a building. Recent scholarship has increasingly challenged this model, showing that architecture is more accurately understood as the outcome of distributed forms of authorship embedded in institutional, technical, and ecological networks.This special issue invites contributions that examine architecture through the lens of collective authorship. Rather than asking who designed a building, the issue asks how architectural ideas emerge through constellations of actors, tools, and institutions. Such approaches foreground invisible or marginalized contributors—clients, consultants, engineers, builders, inhabitants—whose roles are often obscured by professional narratives of individual creativity. They also invite reconsideration of architectural historiography itself: if architectural production is collective, how should architectural history tell its stories?Recent research has demonstrated that many decisive architectural innovations emerged within large organizations rather than from solitary designers. The development of computational methods in architecture, for example, often occurred through technicians and programmers working within corporate firms, leaving traces in documents, software, and engineering systems rather than in conventional narratives of design authorship. At the same time, architectural production increasingly unfolds through transnational partnerships, institutional collaborations, and hybrid design teams that operate across disciplinary and national boundaries.Historians and theorists have begun to expand the range of actors included in architectural narratives. In addition to architects and clients, scholars now examine inhabitants, communities, ideas, technologies, materials, infrastructures, and ecological processes as participants in the making of the built environment. Drawing on work in science and technology studies and environmental humanities—such as Bruno Latour’s analyses of distributed agency, Lorraine Daston’s “biographies of objects,” and Donna Haraway’s concept of sympoiesis—these approaches situate architecture within broader assemblages of human and non-human actors.The aim of this special issue is to gather historical, theoretical, and methodological contributions that rethink architectural authorship as a collective and relational phenomenon—and to reflect on the storytelling methods capable of rendering the drama of collective production visible and legible to wider audiences.Guest Editor: Matthew Allen, Washington University in St. LouisEmail: matthew.a@wustl.eduSpecial Issue Themes1. Invisible Labor and Distributed Agency in Architectural ProductionArchitectural projects are frequently attributed to individual architects or firms, yet their realization depends on extensive networks of collaborators whose contributions remain difficult to see. Technicians, engineers, draftspeople, programmers, project managers, consultants, and construction specialists all shape the design process in ways that traditional narratives of authorship rarely acknowledge.This theme invites papers that recover these hidden or marginalized forms of labor and examine how architectural knowledge circulates within collective environments. Contributions might investigate collaborative design processes within architectural offices, the technical subcultures of engineering and computation, or the ways architectural media translate collective production into simplified narratives of individual creativity. Methodological reflections are equally welcome, including project microhistories, archival reconstruction, oral histories, and ethnographic studies of contemporary practice.2. Rethinking Architectural Narrative: Beyond the Biography of the ArchitectBiography has long served as a central narrative form in architectural history. From the monograph to the retrospective exhibition, the discipline has frequently organized accounts of the built environment around the lives and intentions of individual designers. This approach has also reinforced the idea that architecture originates in singular creative figures.This theme invites contributions that experiment with alternative narrative forms capable of representing collective authorship. While biography remains important, authors are encouraged to explore other storytelling approaches such as collective biographies, object histories, project microhistories, archival narratives, documentary essays, and speculative historiographies. Scholarship on the “biography of objects” in history of science (Lorraine Daston) offers one precedent for expanding narrative frameworks beyond individual lives.3. Bureaucracy, Institutions, and the Organizational Forms of DesignModern architecture is often produced within complex institutional structures: large corporate firms, state design institutes, public agencies, and international consortia. These organizations function through hierarchies, documentation systems, and procedural workflows that shape architectural decisions in ways not always visible in finished buildings.This theme seeks contributions that examine the relationship between architecture and the organizational infrastructures through which it is produced. Papers might analyze the design cultures of large architectural firms, the role of documentation and computation in shaping projects, or the institutional frameworks that enable global architectural production.4. Non-Human Agency and the Expanded Ecology of DesignRecent scholarship in science and technology studies, feminist theory, and environmental humanities emphasizes that agency in design is not limited to human actors. Materials, infrastructures, computational systems, and environmental processes all participate in shaping architectural outcomes.Drawing on perspectives such as Donna Haraway’s concept of sympoiesis—“making-with”—this theme invites contributions examining how non-human actors participate in architectural authorship. Papers may explore the agency of materials, algorithms, environmental forces, or infrastructural systems in shaping architectural form.Manuscript submission information:We invite all those interested to submit materials to the Editorial Office at paujournal@outlook.com using as subject line:CFP Collective Authorship AUTHOR’S SURNAME abstractSubmissions should contain:- Title- Author name(s)- Author affiliation(s)- Contact email address(es)- Short author biography or biographies, maximum 100 words each- Six keywords- Abstract of no more than 500 words- Essential reference list, optional- Up to two key images, optionalThe deadline for submission is November 20th, 2026. Selected authors will be notified by the Editorial Office of Perspectives in Architecture and Urbanism by December 10th, 2026.Selected authors will be invited to present a preliminary draft of their paper (approximately 2,000 to 2,500 words) at an upcoming international seminar hosted by the College of Architecture and Urban Planning (CAUP) of Tongji University in Shanghai (April to May 2027, in-person and online).Full papers must be submitted by July 31st, 2027 following the editorial guidelines of the journal (https://www.keaipublishing.com/en/journals/perspectives-in-architecture-and-urbanism/guide-for-authors/).Selected manuscripts will undergo a double-blind review process and will receive additional feedback from the Guest Editor. Accepted papers will be published online in regular issues of the journal as soon as the review and editing processes are completed. Published texts will be later collected into a virtual special issue, accessible on the journal’s website.Formatting and submission requirementText•	must follow the APA Manual of Style (7th edition)•	spelling should adhere to American convention•	save as Microsoft Word or RTF formatImages•	captions and credits must be included with the submission.

postings.conferenceName: 9th Workshop on Accelerated Machine Learning (AccML)
postings.conferenceText: ==================================================================9th Workshop on Accelerated Machine Learning (AccML)Co-located with the HiPEAC 2027 Conference(https://www.hipeac.net/2027/glasgow/)January 19, 2027Glasgow, United Kingdom==================================================================-------------------------------------------------------------------------CALL FOR CONTRIBUTIONS-------------------------------------------------------------------------Machine learning and AI continue to reshape computing, driving demand for acceleration across the full system stack. The rise of foundation models, generative AI, large language and multimodal models, retrieval-augmented and agentic systems, and capable edge and on-device deployments has expanded accelerated machine learning beyond traditional convolutional networks. Today’s workloads combine dense and sparse computation, long-context attention, recommender systems, graph processing, vision-language reasoning, speech, video, and real-time inference, challenging hardware, software, and programming abstractions. These models are compute-, memory-, communication-, and energy-intensive, making acceleration essential to reduce cost and power consumption in data centers, enable low-latency inference on edge and embedded devices, and support sustainable AI deployment. Progress requires advances in heterogeneous architectures, specialized accelerators, chiplet-based systems, emerging semiconductor and near-/in-memory technologies, low-precision arithmetic, compilers, runtimes, numerical libraries, profiling, benchmarking, and deployment tools. This forum invites contributions on emerging acceleration methods, scalable computation paradigms, hardware/software co-design, and ML/AI-driven design and optimization of efficient and sustainable computing systems.-------------------------------------------------------------------------Links to the Workshop page-------------------------------------------------------------------------Organizers: https://accml.dcs.gla.ac.uk/workshop-2027-hipeac.htmlHiPEAC: https://www.hipeac.net/2027/glasgow/#/program/8325/-------------------------------------------------------------------------Topics-------------------------------------------------------------------------Topics of interest include (but are not limited to):- Novel ML/AI systems: heterogeneous multi-/many-core systems, GPUs, NPUs/TPUs, ASICs, FPGAs, and chiplet-based accelerators;- Software ML/AI acceleration: programming models, languages, primitives, libraries, compilers, runtimes, and frameworks;- Novel ML/AI hardware accelerators and associated system software;- Emerging semiconductor, near-/in-memory, analog, photonic, and neuromorphic technologies for ML/AI hardware acceleration;- ML/AI for the design, optimization, autotuning, and management of hardware, compilers, runtimes, and systems;- Cloud, data-center, edge, embedded, and on-device ML/AI computing: hardware and software to accelerate training and inference;- Hardware/software co-design techniques for efficient model training and inference, including quantization, sparsity, pruning, compression, efficient attention, and distillation;- Training, fine-tuning, serving, and deployment of foundation models, LLMs, multimodal models, large GNNs, recommender systems, agentic AI, and retrieval-augmented generation;-------------------------------------------------------------------------Invited Speakers-------------------------------------------------------------------------Anton Lokhmotov (KRAI): "KRAI's vision on Accelerated Accelerator Programming".Miquel Moreto (BSC): "Designing HPC Architectures to Accelerate AI at BSC"* Other invited speakers will be announced before the paper submission deadline. -------------------------------------------------------------------------Submission-------------------------------------------------------------------------Papers will be reviewed by the workshop's technical program committee according to criteria regarding the submission's quality, relevance to the workshop's topics, and, foremost, its potential to spark discussions about directions, insights, and solutions in the context of accelerating machine learning. Research papers, case studies, and position papers are all welcome.In particular, we encourage authors to submit work-in-progress papers: To facilitate sharing of thought-provoking ideas and high-potential though preliminary research, authors are welcome to make submissions describing early-stage, in-progress, and/or exploratory work in order to elicit feedback, discover collaboration opportunities, and spark productive discussions.The workshop does not have formal proceedings.-------------------------------------------------------------------------Important Dates-------------------------------------------------------------------------Submission deadline: November 13, 2026Notification of decision: November 27, 2026-------------------------------------------------------------------------Organizers-------------------------------------------------------------------------José L. Abellán (University of Murcia)Valentin Radu (University of Sheffield)Ulysse Beaugnon (Google DeepMind)José Cano (University of Glasgow)

postings.conferenceName: AI-Native Software Engineering: Methodologies, Workflows, and Engineering Practices (AISEP)
postings.conferenceText: AI-Native Software Engineering: Methodologies, Workflows, and Engineering Practices (AISEP)The widespread adoption of generative AI is fundamentally changing software engineering. Despite the rapid adoption of AI-powered development tools, organizations continue to rely on ad hoc practices and fragmented workflows, with limited evidence regarding their effectiveness, reliability, and long-term sustainability. There is an increasing need for systematic engineering methodologies, standardized development processes, evaluation frameworks, and best practices that enable the development of robust, trustworthy, and maintainable AI-native software systems. - Purpose of the special issue:This special session aims to bring together researchers and practitioners working on the emerging foundations of AI-native software engineering, with emphasis on evidence-based methodologies, engineering processes, empirical studies, and industrial experiences that advance the maturation of AI-assisted software development.  - Topics of interest: • AI-native software engineering methodologies and frameworks• AI-assisted software development processes and workflows• AI-driven requirements engineering• AI-assisted software architecture and design• AI-supported testing, verification, and validation• Code quality and maintainability of AI-generated software• Human-AI collaboration in software engineering• Metrics and empirical evaluation of AI-assisted development• AI governance, trustworthiness, and security• Industrial case studies and best practices• Standards, guidelines, and engineering frameworks for AI-native software developmentThe objective is to synergise software engineering principles with AI-driven approaches to address emerging challenges of engineering software-intensive systems and provide a forum for disseminating results and building a community of research on AI for SE. - Organizers: • Sokratis Karkalas - University of Derby, UK (contact: s.karkalas-AT-derby.ac.uk) • Aakash Ahmad - University of Derby, UK • Hong Qing (Harry) Yu - University of Derby, UK - Dates:  • Submission Deadline: Nov 10, 2026  • Notification: Dec 10, 2026  • Date of the Session: Jan 15, 2027 - Further details: https://www.icsie.org/cfp_ss1.html

postings.conferenceName: 9th Annual Workshop on Cyber Threat Intelligence and Hunting - in conjuction with IEEE BigData 2026
postings.conferenceText: #About the WorkshopCyberHunt 2026 explores the future of intelligence-driven cyber defence at the intersection of cyber threat intelligence, threat hunting, AI-enabled Security Operations Centres (SOCs), and agentic cybersecurity systems. The workshop brings together researchers and practitioners to discuss methods, tools, architectures, datasets, standards, and operational experiences that make intelligence more actionable, automate security workflows, support human–AI collaboration, and strengthen proactive cyber defence. The workshop will be held for the ninth consecutive year in conjunction with the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData 2026).#Description:Cyber threats are becoming more complex, faster-moving, and increasingly difficult to detect using reactive security approaches alone. Modern Security Operations Centres are therefore shifting towards intelligence-driven, highly automated operations, in which cyber threat intelligence, threat hunting, detection engineering, and incident response are closely integrated to support proactive defence. At the same time, advances in artificial intelligence (AI), large language models (LLMs), agentic systems, and neuro-symbolic reasoning are reshaping how cyber defenders collect, analyse, interpret, and operationalise intelligence. These technologies create new opportunities to automate parts of the intelligence cycle, augment human analysts, improve decision-making, and enable more adaptive security operations. They also introduce new risks, including adversarial manipulation, insecure AI deployment, and AI-enabled cyber threats.The 9th Annual Workshop on Cyber Threat Intelligence and Hunting (CyberHunt 2026) brings together researchers and practitioners from academia, industry, government, and the wider cybersecurity community to explore the evolving relationship between cyber threat intelligence, threat hunting, AI-enabled security operations, and operational cyber defence. The workshop welcomes original research, practical experience reports, system designs, datasets, benchmarks, and emerging ideas that advance intelligence-driven cybersecurity. Particular emphasis is placed on methods and systems that make threat intelligence actionable, support human–AI collaboration, improve SOC automation, enable machine-readable intelligence sharing, and advance rigorous evaluation, effective governance, and the trustworthy deployment of AI-enabled cyber defence systems.#Topics of Interest (please see the comprehensive list on the official webpage):- Threat Intelligence and Threat Hunting- AI, Agentic Systems, and Automation for Cybersecurity- Data, Knowledge Representation, and Intelligence Engineering- SOC Architectures and Operational Intelligence- Security of AI and Adversarial Threats- Emerging Threat Landscapes and Applications- Evaluation, Benchmarking, and Datasets- Governance, Ethics, and Collaboration#Organising Committee:Workshop Chair: - Vasileios Mavroeidis, University of OsloWorkshop Co-Chairs:- Habtamu Abie, Norwegian Computing Center- Nicholas Kolokotronis, University of the Peloponnese- Fabio Martinelli, Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche- Eva Papadogiannaki, Technical University of CreteProgram Committee Chairs:- Mateusz Zych, University of Oslo- Thrasyvoulos Giannakopoulos, University of Piraeus- Vasileios Mavroeidis, University of Oslo#An outstanding paper will be selected for the CyberHunt 2026 Best Paper Award and announced during the workshop#

postings.conferenceName: 6th International Workshop on Distributed Machine Learning for the Intelligent Computing Continuum
postings.conferenceText: 6th International Workshop on Distributed Machine Learning for the Intelligent Computing Continuum (DML-ICC)In conjunction with the 19th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Utility and Cloud Computing (UCC 2026)01-04 December, 2026Florianópolis, Brazilhttp://www.lrc.ic.unicamp.br/dml-icc/### Background ###As the cloud extends to the fog and to the edge, computing services can be scattered over a set of computing resources that encompass users' devices, the cloud, and intermediate computing infrastructure deployed in between. Moreover, increasing networking capacity promises lower delays in data transfers, enabling a continuum of computing capacity that can be used to process large amounts of data with reduced response times. Such large amounts of data are frequently processed through machine learning approaches, seeking to extract knowledge from raw data generated and consumed by a widely heterogeneous set of applications. Distributed machine learning has been evolving as a tool to run learning tasks also at the edge, often immediately after the data is produced, instead of transferring data to the centralized cloud for later aggregation and processing.Following the successful editions of DML-ICC between 2022 and 2025, this fifth edition of DML-ICC keeps the aim to be a forum for discussion among researchers with a distributed machine learning background and researchers from parallel/distributed systems and computer networks. By bringing together these research topics, we look forward in building an Intelligent Computing Continuum, where distributed machine learning models can seamlessly run on any device from the edge to the cloud, creating a distributed computing system that is able to fulfill highly heterogeneous applications requirements and build knowledge from data generated by these applications.### Topics ###DML-ICC 2026 workshop aims to attract researchers from the machine learning community, especially the ones involved with distributed machine learning techniques, and researchers from the parallel/distributed computing communities. Together, these researchers will be able to build resource management mechanisms that are able to fulfill machine learning jobs requirements, but also use machine learning techniques to improve resource management in large distributed systems. Topics of interest include but are not limited to:- Agentic edge and AI agents in the continuum- Autonomic Computing in the Continuum- Business and Cost Models for the Computing Continuum- Complex Event Processing and Stream Processing- Computing and Networking Slicing for the Continuum- Distributed Machine Learning for Resource Management and Scheduling- Distributed Machine Learning in the Computing Continuum- Distributed Machine Learning applications- Distributed Machine Learning performance evaluation- Federated Learning- Intelligent Computing Continuum architectures and models- Management of Distributed Learning tasks- Mobility support in the Computing Continuum- Network management in the Computing Continuum- Privacy using Distributed Learning- Programming models for the Computing Continuum- Resource management and Scheduling in the computing continuum- Smart Environments (Smart Cities, Smart Buildings, Smart Industry, etc.)- Theoretical Modeling for the Computing Continuum### Submissions ###Paper submission through EasyChair:https://easychair.org/conferences/?conf=dmlicc2026The DML-ICC workshop invites authors to submit original and unpublished work. postings.conferenceText: 8th International Conference on Desalination Science and Technology 202714-18 November 2027 | Crowne Plaza Noah Square, Shanghai, ChinaWith growing populations, intensifying climate change, and accelerating urbanization, ensuring a resilient and sustainable freshwater supply is a top global priority—making saline water and wastewater key pathways forward. The 8th International Conference on Desalination Science and Technology 2027 (DESAL 2027), to be held in Shanghai, will connect researchers and industry to advance next-generation desalination beyond conventional membrane approaches by focusing on transport mechanisms, novel desalination materials, innovative hybrid systems, advanced module design, and critical operational strategies (including pre-/post-treatment and membrane fouling control). postings.conferenceText: Call for Papers — AIM-ED 2026Agentic and Inclusive AI for Education: Multi-Agent Systems, Neurodiversity, Intelligent Environments, and Human-Centred LearningSpecial Session S2 at the 3rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Teacher Education (ICAITE 2026)December 6–8, 2026Nagasaki, Japan — Nagasaki UniversityImportant DatesSubmission Deadline: September 20, 2026Notification of Acceptance: October 20, 2026Camera-Ready Paper Due: November 10, 2026Registration Deadline: November 10, 2026Conference: December 6–8, 2026ScopeRecent advances in generative, multimodal, and agentic artificial intelligence are transforming educational technologies from isolated tools into coordinated and adaptive systems capable of supporting teachers, learners, families, patients, and professionals. The AIM-ED 2026 Special Session on Agentic and Inclusive AI for Education aims to bring together researchers and practitioners working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, education, human-computer interaction, learning sciences, healthcare, psychology, cybersecurity, and software engineering. The session particularly welcomes theoretical, technical, methodological, and empirical contributions addressing the design, implementation, and evaluation of agentic, inclusive, secure, and human-centred AI systems for education. A particular focus is placed on AI systems that augment rather than replace human expertise, including trustworthy, explainable, privacy-preserving, and ethically supervised approaches.Topics of InterestTopics include, but are not limited to:- Multi-agent systems and agentic AI for education- LLM-based pedagogical agents and intelligent tutoring systems- Generative AI and autonomous agents in learning environments- Teacher-AI collaboration and AI-assisted educational co-design- AI for neurodivergent learners and students with special educational needs- Inclusive and accessible AI-supported education- Assistive, multimodal, and sensory-adaptive educational technologies- Personalised learning and learner modelling- Adaptive and context-aware educational environments- Educational robotics- Immersive learning and extended reality- Virtual and synthetic learners- Intelligent learning environments- AI-enabled education in smart schools, smart campuses, and smart cities- AI, education, and cybersecurity- Cyber-awareness and protection of educational environments- AI-supported education in healthcare, rehabilitation, oncology, and therapeutic contexts- Explainable AI for education- Fair, ethical, and trustworthy AI- Privacy, safeguarding, and responsible use of educational and health-related data- Human-centred design of educational AI- Evaluation frameworks for agentic and generative AI in education- Case studies and practical experiences in authentic educational and therapeutic settingsSubmission GuidelinesThe official language of ICAITE 2026 is English for both paper submission and presentation.Authors may submit either:Full Papers:Full papers should follow the official ICAITE 2026 template and must be at least 5 pages. Accepted full papers will be invited for presentation and publication.Abstracts:Authors interested in presenting their work without publication may submit an abstract using the conference abstract template.
